item.title: Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers Librería de Satoshi, the technical education organization, recently announced the launch of its global platform as they rebrand to ISMOS and shows off a new website. The organization aims to expand its Bitcoin and open-source developer education program throughout the world, creating local hubs across the world and delivering education programs in local languages. Since 2021, ISMOS has reached more than 3,665 people in more than 40 countries and has financially supported 30 open-source developers, according to a press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine. “Talent is universal; opportunity is not. I founded Librería de Satoshi because I experienced the language barrier in Bitcoin firsthand. ISMOS takes that mission worldwide, so that the next great developer can come from anywhere,” said Dulce Villarreal, CEO and founder of ISMOS. What began as a Bitcoin school for Spanish speakers is today a technical education ecosystem and a complete training path for freedom technologies and open-source developers. ISMOS brings together educators and technology creators: a space to learn and teach with “Freedom Tech values, in more languages, more regions, and more disciplines, with a growing presence in universities, bootcamps, and programming communities.” ISMOS was born in Latin America as Librería de Satoshi and is now a global movement. One Million Bitcoin Developers Around the World ISMOS combines rigorous study programs, direct mentorship, and fellowships in Spanish, Portuguese, and English, and soon in more languages. Subjects will include Bitcoin, cryptography, cybersecurity, mathematics, AI, Nostr, open-source software, and open AI models. The platform is open source, and software developers can explore its open tools at github.com/ismos-xyz . Today ISMOS is primarily supported by Btrust and the Human Rights Foundation. Other organizations, such as OpenSats and the Gemini Opportunity Fund, have supported its work in the past with smaller grants, according to the press release. The announcement reflects nearly five years of growth and a deeper commitment to equal opportunity. “Someone coding in Argentina, Nigeria, or El Salvador deserves the same chance to build a first-class technical career as anyone in Silicon Valley or London.” SMOS aims to go beyond study programs to provide individual support to the best developers through programs such as B4OS (Bitcoin 4 Open Source), fellowships, and its developer residencies: “in their language, at their level, and with the specific support they need to go further than they imagined.” Press contact Karina Conde, Director of Operations. comms@ismos.xyz This post Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Juan Galt .

item.title: A dyslexia diagnosis can help struggling children, but what about the rest?
item.description: Shutterstock/Jakub Krechowicz In years gone by, children who struggled to learn to read and spell were labelled “stupid”, “lazy” or “dim”. Today, of course, we are much more enlightened – now we label many of these children as “dyslexic”. But perhaps this label is still a bad idea. Picture two 9-year-olds reading at the level of an average 6-year-old. One gets a diagnosis of dyslexia. This positively affects her wellbeing. Her teachers now understand she has dyslexia and that she can get tailored help. The other child isn’t so lucky. Maybe his parents can’t afford a dyslexia test – in the UK, assessment isn’t available on the NHS and can cost several hundred pounds. In the US it could set parents back thousands of dollars. Or perhaps he was tested but the result was negative. Until very recently, this outcome was common for already disadvantaged children, because the official definition of dyslexia included the idea of “discrepancy” – that reading problems should be unexpected given a child’s other cognitive abilities. Assessing ability using IQ tests can also be biased against those from lower socioeconomic groups or learning to read in a second language. By extension, this second child is just bad at reading or lazy, or both, and not eligible to receive extra help with reading. Advertisement Two children with the same learning difficulty. One gets help, the other does not Two children with the same learning difficulty. One gets help and understanding and the other doesn’t, all because of a label. Yet this label is based on a questionable assessment. Despite trials using a wide range of cognitive processes, researchers have been unable to find meaningful ways to identify dyslexia. So, why not just help all children who struggle to read? Each has a unique combination of risk and remediation factors, but all will benefit most if we intervene when the problem first shows up, instead of waiting years for them to fail and then receive a diagnosis. Our newfound understanding of what is happening in their brains even suggests some surprisingly simple ways to help . Giving every child the best possible chance to overcome their challenge is what matters, not the label we attach to them.

item.title: The DNA is backwards on The Selfish Gene’s cover – again
item.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Don’t get it twisted Feedback is not young. We have been here on the back pages for many years, endlessly pushing a boulder up a hill and trying to take joy in the effort. This means, every so often, we are forced to repeat ourselves – because the world repeats itself. With a due sense of ennui, we turn our world-weary eyes to the cover of the new 50th anniversary edition of Richard Dawkins’s popular science classic The Selfish Gene . The title, written in all-caps, takes up most of the cover. The “I” in “SELFISH” has been replaced by a colourful little drawing of a DNA double helix. Advertisement Alas, something is awry. Geneticist Simon Fisher pointed it out on Bluesky : “You know a gene is selfish when its DNA twists the wrong way, as demonstrated by the left-handed double-helix proudly adorning the 50th Anniversary Edition of the multimillion copy bestseller on this topic.” Yes, once again we have an example of a DNA molecule being drawn, essentially, backwards. In reality, it is a right-handed double helix, but the one on the book cover is left-handed. It’s twisting the wrong way. Feedback’s mind’s eye immediately cast itself back to March 2025 , when we covered a Lego model that included many scientific and technological objects, including a sadly left-handed DNA. It turns out that The Selfish Gene ‘s art has been wrong for at least a decade. Patrick Goymer , an editor at PLOS One , shared the cover of the 40th anniversary edition on Bluesky, and it has the same left-handed DNA in place of the “I”. Feedback notes that our own copy is the 30th anniversary edition, and the DNA is correct. At some point since 2006, the DNA on the cover has flipped into a mirror universe. This little mistake would be doubly embarrassing if, say, the Nobel prize in chemistry had recently been awarded for research into these sorts of mirror molecules. Can you imagine? Coca-Cola faecaloma Sometimes a scientific paper has a title so vivid, so immediate, that Feedback just has to write about it. Such is the case with a paper published in Cureus , titled: “Massive fecaloma dissolved by Coca-Cola: A case report”. It was sent to us by Australia reporter Alice Klein, who either has a truly terrible browser history or makes extensive use of a VPN. A faecaloma, for those not yet blessed with the knowledge, is a large lump of impacted faeces trapped in a person’s rectum. In this case report, the faecaloma had a maximum diameter of 12.2 centimetres. Readers anxious to see a dramatisation of such a condition are advised to try series two , episode five of The Pitt , in which one of the patients has impacted faeces that the doctors must manually dislodge. Based on our own personal experience, we do not recommend watching this sequence over dinner. item.title: 2027: We won’t endorse any candidate — Health workers
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 elections, the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) on Wednesday declared that its members will not endorse or finance any candidate. The health workers also said they are rejecting a spectator role in the forthcoming elections and demanded binding commitments on CONHESS and outstanding arrears. Speaking in his welcome address at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Abuja, the President of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, Comrade Kabiru Ado Sani, said the union will enter the 2027 general election neither as party loyalists nor as passive observers, but as an organised constituency demanding enforceable commitments on welfare, CONHESS arrears, and outstanding collective agreements. In a strongly worded position ahead of the polls, the union said the question confronting health workers is no longer whether they will participate in the election, but on what terms. “The permutation is now upon us. The question is no longer whether health workers will be in it, but whether we shall be in it as spectators, as foot soldiers, or as a constituency with a strong position,” the MHWUN President said. He warned that health workers must not allow their numerical strength and professional importance to be reduced to election-season mobilisation for politicians who may abandon their concerns afterwards. MHWUN insisted that it remains a trade union, not a political party, and would not endorse any candidate or political platform. “MHWUN is a trade union, not a political party. We will not endorse any party or candidate, and the funds of this Union will not be used to finance any of them,” the union leader stated. He added that members remain free to vote according to their conscience, stressing that no individual has the authority to speak for the union while campaigning for a party. “Our members are free to vote their conscience, and no one speaks for this Union when speaking for a party,” he said. The union argued that its political influence should not depend on telling members whom to vote for, but on forcing every contender for power to confront the health sector’s unresolved demands. “Our influence does not lie in telling members how to vote. It lies in making the health worker’s agenda impossible to ignore, whoever wins,” the MHWUN political head declared. He explained that at the centre of that agenda are the CONHESS salary structure, unpaid arrears, and collective agreements reached with the Federal Government but yet to be fully implemented. The union framed its demands in legal as well as moral terms, insisting that agreements signed by the Federal Government cannot be treated as disposable political promises. “A collective agreement signed by the Federal Government is an obligation of the State,” Dr. Sani said. “It does not lapse when a tenure ends, and no incoming administration is entitled to treat it as the debt of its predecessor.” He wa

item.title: Democrats to Target Trump’s Crypto Ventures After Taking Congress
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Democrats to Target Trump’s Crypto Ventures After Taking Congress House Democrats plan to open investigations into President Donald Trump’s family crypto businesses once they take control in January, with World Liberty Financial, its Emirati investor and the pardon of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao at the top of the list. Rep. Robert Garcia of California, who will chair the House Oversight Committee, answered the Associated Press call with a two-word statement at 3:18 a.m.: “Lawyer up.” His office said he intends to take on what it calls the “Trump Crime Family” alongside corporate corruption, immigration enforcement abuses and the Epstein files. Garcia told Punchbowl News the committee will examine the family’s crypto deals, Donald Trump Jr.’s business dealings and relatives such as Jared Kushner “sitting on boards and getting contracts.” The difference from the past two years is subpoena power. Democrats have written letters, requested Treasury probes and held shadow hearings; the majority lets them compel documents and testimony from the administration and from private companies without the president’s consent. Reuters reported in September that inquiries could begin as early as February, with corporate donors to the White House ballroom and firms that did deals with Trump relatives among the first targets. World Liberty Financial, the DeFi and stablecoin venture the Trump family launched in September 2024, is expected to come first. Democrats have focused on a $500 million investment by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE national security adviser, whose vehicle took a reported 49% stake shortly before the January 2025 inauguration. The stake matters because World Liberty is seeking a federal trust bank charter for its USD1 stablecoin; the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted conditional approval on Aug. 14, with final sign-off pending. Tahnoon’s group and a Trump-affiliated entity together control about 87% of the bank’s holding company, according to The Wall Street Journal. House Democrats asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in February to investigate the deal and sought suspicious activity reports tied to the family’s ventures. Those requests carried no legal force. Senate Democrats on the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, led by Richard Blumenthal, opened their own inquiry into the TRUMP token and World Liberty earlier this year. The second target is the October 2025 pardon of Zhao, whose exchange helped launch USD1 and was hacked for $6.34 billion last week. Zhao has said he has no business ties to the Trump family and did not discuss clemency with them. Trump’s 2025 financial disclosure listed more than $1 billion in crypto-related income, including about $635 million in TRUMP memecoin royalties; Reuters put the family’s crypto earnings at $2.3 billion or more. item.title: Anthony Rizzo shares urgent MLB lockout warning amid salary cap dilemma
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Anthony Rizzo shares urgent MLB lockout warning amid salary cap dilemma appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . MLB unfortunately seems to be headed for a lockout. Players and owners are on completely different sides of the salary cap debate . There are other topics that will impact the new collective bargaining agreement discussions, but the salary cap is the most pressing issue at the moment. The MLBPA as well as MLB will continue to look for solutions , but a lockout will occur if a new deal isn’t reached by early December. Former MLB star Anthony Rizzo shared his thoughts on the topic during a recent segment of Ross and Rizzo Unfiltered. “Look, no one wants to lose baseball,” Rizzo said. “… Baseball is in a great spot, it’s very competitive. But with this lockout, with the owners digging down and saying they’re going salary cap, I need fans to understand, forever baseball hasn’t had a salary cap. There’s so much that needs to happen in this CBA negotiation that this could drag out unfortunately longer than expected.” Baseball would be dealt a brutal blow if games end up being missed due to the lockout. The game is indeed in a “great spot” right now as Rizzo mentioned. If the situation does end up dragging out “longer than expected” like Rizzo said, baseball will be in an especially challenging position. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB has worked hard to bounce back after it seemed as if the sport’s popularity was trending in the wrong direction not too long ago. The rule changes to the game such as the pitch clock and ABS challenge system have seemingly led to an increase in fan interest in the sport once again. So, what may it take for the owners and players to put their differences aside and find a solution? Rizzo, who, again, was a star at the MLB level, admitted money could be the breaking point. “But until there’s an actual deadline, until owners start losing money — which is not going to be for a long time into the lockout — or players start feeling it on their paychecks, things aren’t going to start moving unfortunately.” Rizzo surely hopes he’s wrong about things potentially taking longer than anticipated to resolve, but his take should not be overlooked. item.title: Nigeria can become Africa’s rice export hub — NGF
item.description: …Forum says 5.3m-tonne production deficit can be bridged, urges states to establish data banks By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has expressed optimism that Nigeria can become a major rice exporter in Africa, insisting that the country’s agricultural potential and available human, financial and natural resources are sufficient to achieve the ambition. The forum said Nigeria could close its 5.3 million metric tonnes rice production deficit and become a net exporter if governments addressed policy inconsistencies, improved agricultural data and provided sustained support to farmers and other players across the value chain. The Director-General of the NGF, Dr. Abdulateef Shittu, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja during the launch of the Northwest Rice Diagnostic Report organised by the forum. Shittu said Nigeria currently consumed about 8.6 million metric tonnes of rice annually, a figure projected to rise to 9.1 million metric tonnes next year, while domestic production stood at only 3.3 million metric tonnes. He blamed the production shortfall on inconsistent government policies, poor coordination and other challenges affecting the agricultural sector. According to him, Nigeria has no justification for remaining dependent on imported rice, given its agricultural resources and capacity to supply regional African markets and parts of Europe. He cited China’s transition from food deficit to self-sufficiency through targeted investments, saying Nigeria needed similar political commitment to achieve food security. Shittu said: “You can see the huge gap. So, how do we address this? There are a lot of policy flip-flops, policy mismatch, and quite a number of other challenges that we will all have to address. But my motto simply is that there is no problem without a solution. “We have all the resources, both human and material. We have the land and everything that we need to support farmers and other actors across the value chain. Whatever they need can be guaranteed.” He described credible data as central to agricultural planning and disclosed that the NGF had established a dedicated data department to improve the collection and management of information across states. He urged all 36 states to establish functional Bureaus of Statistics, noting that Kaduna and some other states had already taken the initiative. According to him, national statistics, including Gross Domestic Product figures, should reflect aggregated data from the states and the Federal Capital Territory. The NGF boss said the forum was also challenging figures presented by development partners where it believed they were inaccurate. “If we are saying it is not correct, we have to show them which one is correct,” he said. He added that heads of State Bureaus of Statistics met quarterly under a committee of practice, while commissioners of agriculture also held periodic meetings to exchange ideas and experiences. item.title: Survey: Will the NY Giants win the NFC East?
item.description: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy and defensive lineman Shelby Harris celebrate a win | Getty Images The New York Giants return to action this week after a much-needed bye week. The Giants are preparing to go on the road to play the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9. And for the first time in a long time, the Giants come into this game as road favorites over the Eagles (3.5-point favorites, per FanDuel ). The 4-2-1 Giants currently have a 1.5-game lead in the NFC East over the 3-5 Dallas Cowboys and are currently the (slight) favorites to win the division. The conversation around the Giants has shifted dramatically since the preseason, going from whether they’ll show progress in John Harbaugh’s first season to whether the Giants will get their first division crown since 2011. Looking ahead, the Giants face some stuff tests. Their final 10 games are: at Eagles (2-6) vs. Washington Commanders (2-4-1) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) at Indianapolis Colts (2-6) vs. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) at Seattle Seahawks (4-4) vs. Cleveland Browns (5-3) at Detroit Lions (5-2) at Cowboys (3-5) vs. Eagles (2-6) The Giants’ tie with the Commanders complicates matters for the Giants’ division rivals. If New York can go 5-5 over the final 10 weeks and finish with a 9-7-1 record, the Cowboys would need to go 7-2 over the same stretch. It’s obviously difficult to forecast games a month, or even a week, down the road. However, we want to ask the Big Blue View community simply and directly: Will the New York Football Giants win the NFC East? Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Giants fans and fans across the country. Will the Giants win the East? Are you confident in the Giants? item.title: Joe Scarborough goes after ESPN’s Pat McAfee: ‘It is a shame for the viewer’
item.description: Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” Joe Scarborough of “Morning Joe” hammered away at Tuesday during election day. McAfee’s recent headline-grabbing issues with the University of Utah was the tipping point. “I’ve just had enough of this Pat McAfee ruining ‘College GameDay,’” Scarborough said Tuesday. “I look forward to waking up on Saturday mornings and watching that. ... It’s like he’s melting down. ... “It’s really ESPN. I mean, they run their company the way they want to run their company, but man, it is a shame for the viewer.” It's election day in America, and Morning Joe spent over two minutes discussing the country's most pressing issue: Pat McAfee ruining College GameDay "I don't know if they haven't gotten the message yet, but the manosphere that we all thought was brought in in '24, it may get… pic.twitter.com/a16be985Zt — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 3, 2026 McAfee revealed there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversy surrounding ESPN’s “College GameDay” visit to Utah. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but ... I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee posted on X. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.” The post includes screenshots from direct messages threatening violence against him and tweets expressing a desire to see him dead. The issue, according to Scarborough, is the show has gotten away from college football being played on Saturday and it’s more about itself. “I love watching Rece (Davis),” he said. “I love watching those guys and watching Nick (Saban) on there talking. ... Kirk Herbstreit’s amazing. Desmond (Howard) — they’re all great. And they’re all being eclipsed by ESPN’s just insatiable desire to give this guy more time.” “Maybe you aren’t having to be yelling at people and being freaked out because two kids in Utah put up signs or say something that might offend you,” Scarborough said. Meanwhile, McAfee said he felt “uncomfortable” after the University of Utah posted a since-deleted video of students “dogging” him. He also said the video shared by the university account was inciteful against him. McAfee cited the visit to the University of Utah reminded him of assassination of Charlie Kirk . Utah, for its part, apologized Monday. item.title: Yusuf urges Nigerians to be patient with Tinubu’s policies
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has urged Nigerians to be patient with President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the difficult decisions taken by the administration are aimed at rescuing the economy and stabilising its macroeconomic environment. The governor said the policies had helped stabilise the economy, expressing optimism that the benefits would eventually translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. Yusuf, who was represented by Muhammad Yusuf Jamu, spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of campaign coordinators for the presidential, governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections in Tarauni Local Government Area of Kano State. He said the President had taken difficult decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, adding that economic stability would create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive. “The President’s economic policies have helped rescue the country’s economy and stabilise the macroeconomy. With a stable economy, businesses can go to the markets and carry out their transactions. “We are now at a stage where the economy is growing, and the microeconomy will soon begin to flourish, so that Nigerians can also feel the benefits. “We are in a period where tough decisions have been taken to rescue the country. We urge Nigerians to be patient with the President and his government’s policies. At the end of the day, we will all celebrate,” he said. The governor also urged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano to sustain efforts towards reconciliation and unity within the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. He called on party members to abide by established rules and work collectively towards the success of the APC. “I urge you to continue on this path of reconciliation and strictly adhere to the rules of the game. We have the best candidates to present to the people of Kano,” he said. He further urged party supporters to vote for the APC across all elective positions in the 2027 elections. “On election day, everyone should vote for the APC from top to bottom and from bottom to top,” he added. Also speaking, the APC candidate for Tarauni Federal Constituency, Hon. Nasir Bala Aminu Ja’oji, pledged to expand empowerment programmes and educational support for residents if elected in 2027. Ja’oji said education would remain his priority, alongside youth and women development, healthcare and economic empowerment. He disclosed that he had supported 2,500 beneficiaries across the 10 wards of Tarauni with N125 million in cash grants and distributed 100 motorcycles to constituents. He also said he had paid registration fees for students sitting the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE), Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations, as well as provided financial assistance to hundreds of students in tertiary institutions. “If elected, I

item.title: Canucks: Overreaction trade Vancouver must make to increase lottery odds
item.description: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Canucks: Overreaction trade Vancouver must make to increase lottery odds appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Almost nothing is going right for the Vancouver Canucks in the early stages of the 2026-27 NHL season, as they suffered their 13th regulation loss in just 17 games on Tuesday evening, continuing their extremely tough start to the campaign. Their latest defeat came at the hands of divisional rival Anaheim Ducks, who held on for a 5-4 victory at Rogers Arena in downtown Vancouver, leaving the Canucks three points behind the next-lowest team, the Los Angeles Kings, in the Pacific Division standings. One of Vancouver’s regular contributors so far this season is forward Elias Pettersson, who picked up a pair of assists as part of the loss to the Ducks, increasing his total to 14 so far in 17 games played. As of now, Pettersson is on pace to rebound to 20 goals and 69 assists, which would give him his highest point total since reaching 89 points in 2023-24. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) However, it’s time for Canucks general manager Ryan Johnson, who took over the role during the summer from the fired Patrik Allvin, to give more serious consideration to trading the Swedish star forward, given the fact that all signs point toward the Canucks once again being a lottery team this season . Canucks need to finally trade Elias Pettersson and recoup assets Bob Frid-Imagn Images Pettersson has been one of the most talked-about players in trade rumors over the past year. Last season, the Canucks made several significant moves, including trading captain and former Norris Trophy-winning defenseman Quinn Hughes to the Minnesota Wild. They also traded forwards Conor Garland and Kiefer Sherwood, as well as defenseman Tyler Myers. Pettersson, however, remained in Vancouver. The prevailing belief is that his $11.6 million salary cap hit has discouraged potential suitors, especially given that his production has declined in recent seasons. It’s encouraging, though, to see Pettersson producing at a pace that more closely resembles the player Vancouver paid him to be when they signed him to the aforementioned extension. Still, his talents could be better utilized by a team with legitimate Stanley Cup aspirations rather than a club that can realistically start planning its summer vacation by February. The Canucks finished last in the NHL standings last season but ultimately fell to third in the draft lottery. That cost them the opportunity to select consensus No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna, who was taken by the Toronto Maple Leafs. Vancouver instead used its pick on forward Caleb Malhotra, the son of head coach Manny Malhotra. As Vancouver and other NHL teams have learned in recent years, finishing last doesn’t guarantee the first overall pick. item.title: Braden Smith’s 19-Point Start Proves Pacers Depth Is Broken
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Braden Smith just showed the NBA what happens when a team runs out of stars. The rookie from Purdue scored 19 points and handed out 10 assists in a game where the Indiana Pacers started six players because everyone else was hurt or resting. The Hawks managed to escape with a 108-104 win on Monday night, but they nearly got upset by a squad that was missing its entire starting lineup. This loss for Atlanta feels like a lucky escape rather than a dominant performance, and the numbers tell the whole story. A Salary Gap That Makes No Sense The financial disparity in this game was absurd. According to Peachtree Hoops , bench players totaled roughly $193 million in salary, whereas active roster members earned approximately $15 million. That is a difference of nearly $200 million between the bench and the active roster. The Pacers were forced to play three players on two-way contracts just to get a game in. Tyrese Haliburton and TJ McConnell were among the names missing, leaving Smith as the only pure point guard available. He stepped up and ran the offense like a veteran, proving the team has depth but lacks the payroll flexibility to keep everyone healthy. Atlanta had their own issues to deal with. Jalen Johnson was sidelined with an ankle tweak, and Jock Landale also missed out. Even with these absences, the Hawks held on, but it was closer than it should have been. Nickeil Alexander-Walker led the way with 34 points and hit nine three-pointers to tie his career best. Hawks head coach Quin Snyder admitted the win was tough to earn. “It’s a really good win,” said Snyder postgame, acknowledging the team was not at their best inside the rim. Smith Earns More Minutes Immediately Braden Smith did not just survive his first start; he dominated it. He spent 42 minutes on the floor and shot 8 of 13 from the field. Before this game, he had played only 18 total NBA minutes and scored a single point. He found out at walk-through that he would start, yet he attacked the basket with confidence. He scored 18 points in the paint by halftime, showing he can finish through contact even without Ivica Zubac or Pascal Siakam. 8 Points 9 Seconds reported that Smith performed exceptionally well during Monday night’s matchup versus the Atlanta Hawks. The Pacers have a problem with their injury report, but they have found a solution in their rookie. Smith is the only player who can run the offense right now, and his performance proves he deserves more opportunity. The Hawks will have to prepare for a team that is dangerous even when missing its stars. Atlanta improved to 4-4, but the Pacers fell to 2-6 despite putting up a massive fight. The Hawks Need to Fix Their Clutch Game Atlanta built double-digit leads multiple times, only to watch them vanish. The Hawks shot 28 percent from the field in the third quarter and went on a nearly four-minute field goal drought in the fourth. Onyeka Okongwu sealed the win with a hook shot with 10 seconds lef

item.title: Sixers And Pistons Clash In Detroit With Top Records On Line
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers and Detroit Pistons are set to meet in Detroit on Wednesday night with both teams holding the best records in the Eastern Conference. This matchup features two squads that have made a strong statement early in the season. The 76ers enter the game with a 7-1 record, while the Pistons sit at 6-1. Both teams have won their last four games, setting the stage for a high-stakes battle for positioning in the East. Joel Embiid is expected to play despite dealing with right foot plantar fasciitis. He was not listed on the initial injury report for Wednesday’s contest, according to PhillyVoice . The star center sat out the final quarter of Monday’s game against the Chicago Bulls to manage his condition. His return is a major boost for a team that has started the season on a historic run. Embiid Finds His Rhythm Embiid has been dealing with foot pain that flares up at times. He admitted the issue is painful and requires careful management. After the game, “I was on minutes restriction,” Embiid explained why he sat out the end of the third quarter and the entire final frame. Despite the struggle, he contributed 15 points and eight rebounds in 25 minutes during the win over Chicago. The Sixers center is also adjusting to a new role where he is not the only focal point of the offense. He has had to get used to not touching the ball every possession. “I’m such a rhythm guy,” Embiid said. “And over the years, obviously, I’ve had a lot of opportunities to just touch the ball almost every other possession.” This adjustment has been part of the team’s success, as the starting lineup combined for 102 points in the last win. Pistons Rely on Defense Detroit has built its success on a tough defensive identity. In their last four victories, opponents have been held under 95 points by the Pistons. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff believes this style makes them a dangerous team when their shots are falling. “When we are defending at the level that we are capable of defending, and the shots are going, we are going to be a tough out,” Bickerstaff said. Cade Cunningham has led the way with 33 points and seven assists in their last win over Charlotte. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jalen Duren is out with an injury, leaving the Pistons without their starting center. The Detroit center remains sidelined with a hamstring strain. This absence removes a key interior presence that the Sixers would normally have to face. The Pistons also lost sharpshooter Isaiah Joe to injury. Despite these losses, the team has shown they can win with depth and star power from Cunningham. Early Season Stakes This game carries extra weight because of the lone blemish on Philadelphia’s record. The Pistons beat the 76ers 106-93 on the road on Oct. 25. item.title: Spurs face three big decisions with January looming
item.description: Spurs face three big decisions with January looming Tottenham Academy Loans in Focus as Luca Gunter Eyes January Move Tottenham’s season is beginning to gather a little rhythm under Roberto De Zerbi and, in the background, another important story is developing, one that often tells you just as much about a club’s health as events on a Saturday afternoon. According to Standard , young goalkeeper Luca Gunter is set to assess his loan options in January after being recalled from Boreham Wood last month. It is a small detail on the surface, but it speaks to a wider truth about how modern clubs try to bridge the gap between academy promise and senior football reality. Gunter had embedded himself quickly at Boreham Wood, becoming first choice and playing a prominent role in a side that has made an unbeaten start in the National League. Those are not throwaway appearances, they are the kind of matches that begin to harden a young player and teach him the weight of responsibility. Luca Gunter Recall Creates Fresh Tottenham Decision The recall came after an injury to third-choice goalkeeper Brandon Austin, with Gunter returning to train around the first team at Spurs. The expectation is that he will remain in that environment for now before looking to head back out on loan when the January window opens. That feels sensible. A goalkeeper’s development can stall in a hurry if minutes disappear, and while exposure to senior training at Tottenham has obvious value, competitive football remains the currency that matters most. Tottenham Academy Prospects Facing January Choices Gunter is not the only one weighing his next step. Tyrese Hall is expected to attract both loan and permanent interest, while Under-21s captain James Rowswell could also seek a move after failing to secure one in the summer. These are the sorts of decisions that can shape a career long before the wider public has fully noticed a player’s name. Photo IMAGO There are encouraging signs, too. De Zerbi has shown a growing willingness to involve academy players as results have improved, and Luca Williams-Barnett was handed his Premier League debut against Crystal Palace. Others, including Tye Hall and Callum Olusesi, have also been brought closer to the senior set-up. Roberto De Zerbi Pathway Offers Spurs Encouragement For Tottenham, this is the balancing act. Keep the best young talent close enough to feel the standards of the first team, but brave enough to let them go elsewhere for the matches that make them. Gunter’s next move may look modest from afar, yet these are often the decisions that help decide whether an academy produces hopefuls or genuine first-team players. Our View This is the kind of update that catches the eye because it hints at a club trying to become smarter with its young talent. There is something reassuring about seeing a goalkeeper like Gunter trusted enough to be first choice on loan, then valued enough to be pulled back into the first-team picture when needed. That

item.title: An inside look at Nationals prospect Jarlin Susana’s Arizona Fall League campaign
item.description: TUCSON, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 10: Jarlin Susana #91 of the Washington Nationals pitches during a game between the Salt River Rafters and the Scottsdale Scorpions at Kino Veterans Memorial Stadium on Saturday, October 10, 2026 in Tucson, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is not a whole lot of baseball going on right now, but there still is one league that is playing. The Arizona Fall League is a great opportunity for prospects to either prove themselves or make up for lost time. Nats prospect Jarlin Susana falls into both of those categories. He is coming off an injury that cost him several months, and he wants to compete. Through the SB Nation network, I was able to get Susana’s perspective on things. Samantha Bradford, of the Rockies site Purple Row was out in Arizona, and I was able to ask Susana questions through her. Luis Sanchez of World Baseball Network did a great job as Susana’s interpreter as well. Here is a full transcript of the interview. A big part of Susana’s game is his massive velocity, and that is something he is clearly aware of. One of the things he said he was most proud of this season was breaking the AFL velocity record. Susana has actually thrown the 9 hardest pitches in AFL history. He told us that the record was not something he was actively trying to set, but he was happy he accomplished it. 103.8 MPH! 🤯 Jarlin Susana owns the 9 fastest pitches in AFL history! 20 K in 16 IP across 5 starts. The Nats have a monster coming. 🔥 Future ace or closer? pic.twitter.com/DHnQSpWper — natsfanatics (@natsfanatics_) October 29, 2026 While Susana averages over 100 MPH, he said that his curveball is his best pitch. On TJstat’s pitch tracking site, it has Susana throwing a slider, a sweeper and a curve. However, the shapes of all three pitches look very similar, so I think those are all one pitch. Since Susana calls it a curveball, that is what we will call it. That classification is actually interesting to me. On most sites, that pitch is called a slider. However, Susana calls it a curve and the shape has more drop than your average slider but less than most curveballs. It is a bit of a slurve to me. Whatever you want to call it, the pitch is nasty and generates whiffs over half the time. Interestingly, Susana said the reason that his curve is so good is because of how well it pairs with his fastball. He told us that “pitching alongside my fastball makes my curveball elite”. Having pitches that tunnel off each other and look similar out of the hand is a great trait to have. One other thing that Susana was proud of during his AFL campaign was winning Arizona Fall League pitcher of the week. He told us that was one of his goals, and he accomplished it. The AFL is usually a hitter friendly environment, so Susana having success there is impressive. Congratulations to our week one NFP Pitcher of the Week, Jarlin Susana. item.title: Defeat ends Djokovic's hopes of making ATP Finals
item.description: Djokovic's 24 Grand Slam singles titles are a men's record but have him tied with Margaret Court overall [Getty Images] Novak Djokovic is out of the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin after a second-round defeat by qualifier Rinky Hijikata at the Paris Masters. It means Djokovic, 39, has failed to qualify for the event for only the second time in the past 20 seasons when fit. The Serb likely needed to reach the semi-finals in Paris to qualify, although the draw had appeared to open up for him after two of his rivals for a place fell earlier in the day. Despite a good start, Djokovic was unable to repel Australian world number 83 Hijikata in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat. As Hijikata lifted his level at the end of the second set and throughout the decider, Djokovic, who appeared laboured and to be struggling physically, produced a series of errors, bringing an end to his season. Zverev annoyed by reaction to becoming world number one Death threats for Briton Burrage on WTA Tour return Despite reaching the final of the Australian Open and the semi-finals of Wimbledon, Djokovic has not reached the quarter-final in any of this year's Masters 1000 events. He won the last of his 24 Grand Slam titles at the US Open in 2023. Qualifying for Turin would have given him a chance to win a record-extending eighth title at the season-ending championships. Instead, only Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul remain in contention to take the final two places currently held by Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar. Djokovic had not failed to qualify when fit since 2017. Tiafoe's chances were taken out of his hands earlier on Wednesday when he fell to a 6-3 1-6 7-6 (11-9) defeat by Frenchman Quentin Halys. Australian Alex de Minaur then failed to take advantage as he lost 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 to Argentine Tomas Martin Etcheverry. A run in Paris could have secured De Minaur's qualification. Elsewhere, world number one Alexander Zverev and fourth seed Daniil Medvedev, both of whom have already qualified for Turin, were also beaten. Zverev said he was "annoyed" by the response to him becoming world number one after a straight-sets loss to Lorenzo Musetti while Medvedev was beaten 6-4 6-4 by Peruvian world number 33 Ignacio Buse. item.title: Tom Brady Returns To Foxborough As Fox Broadcaster
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The moment fans have waited six years is finally here. Tom Brady returns to Foxborough on Sunday not as the man in the huddle, but as the voice in the booth. Erin Andrews is already stoking the fire for this massive homecoming. She posted the official hype video on her Instagram story with zero words, letting the moment speak for itself per Yahoo Sports . He told Colin Cowherd on Tuesday that the experience will be “certainly emotional.” The legend spent two decades walking every inch of that stadium, from the locker rooms to the meeting rooms. Before moving to Tampa in 2020, he guided the Patriots to six titles and nine Super Bowl appearances. Now he returns to call a game against the Green Bay Packers. It is a strange role for a man who once held the fate of the franchise in his hands. The View From The Booth Brady will sit alongside Kevin Burkhardt for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. This marks his first time calling a Patriots game since joining Fox Sports in 2022. Andrews and Tom Rinaldi will handle the sideline work. The setup feels right for a team that just beat Miami 24-19. Brady admitted he is “very, very excited” to be there in front of a friendly home crowd. He noted that the Packers are a team he already covered this year and knows well. The matchup features two 5-3 teams. Fox made the game official early this week, releasing a preview that fans have been waiting for. A New Perspective on the Patriots What makes this return unique is Brady’s new take on the current squad. He praised the 2026 Patriots for starting slow and then going on a tear. He called quarterback Drake Maye an MVP candidate after the team faced the Seahawks in the Super Bowl last February. “I’m really talking about this awesome program that’s been built,” Brady said. According to him, the Patriots consistently manage to execute things correctly. He will be calling a game that includes his former team and must remain impartial. The bias test begins when he puts on the headset. Brady’s contract with Fox is a reported 10-year, $375 million deal. He must remain impartial while covering a team he once played for. But Brady seems ready to handle the pressure.

item.title: Lee Westwood Says He Is Unemployed Amid LIV Golf Uncertainty
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Lee Westwood admits he has no job in professional golf right now. The 53-year-old Englishman told The Chipping Forecast podcast that he is currently unemployed. He has not signed a contract for the new LIV Golf structure, nor has he agreed to return to the DP World Tour. This leaves a former World No. 1 in a unique position with no tour to play on. The uncertainty stems from a major shift in the golf world. LIV Golf is moving to a new model called LIV 2.0 without funding from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. Several big names have already left the league. Westwood says he will not sign up until the details make sense for him. A Clear Deadline and a Long Ban Westwood faces a hard choice with a specific date attached to it. He must notify the DP World Tour by November 12 if he wants to rejoin for the 2027 season. The catch is a severe punishment for leaving the tour in 2022. According to The Straits Times, returning would mean serving a 10-tournament suspension. This suspension blocks him from playing until the spring. Westwood explained the timeline clearly on the podcast. “I know that if I sign up on the 12th of November, I’ve then got to serve a 10-tournament suspension, which takes me through the South African Open,” he said. The first event he could play would be the Turkish Airlines Open in the first week of May. That is a long time to sit on the sidelines. A player of Westwood’s age does not have many years left. Missing five months of competitive golf is a big risk. He has already looked at the schedule and sees the gap. “I’ve looked at the schedule, and I feel like the first event I could play in on the DP World Tour will be the Turkish Airlines Open,” he told GolfMagic . He has not looked past that date yet. Why LIV 2.0 Has Not Worked The new version of LIV Golf has failed to secure deals with its top players. Westwood is among those who have walked away from the table. Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, and Tyrrell Hatton are also not returning. The league lost its main financial backer, which changed the entire game. Westwood is blunt about the offers he has received. “There’s nothing that’s been presented to me that was agreeable for LIV 2.0,” he told The Straits Times. He notes that many details still need to be fixed. Deadlines have passed without him hearing whether he must sign or not. “There are still a lot of things that would need fine-tuning; deadlines have come and gone, and I’ve heard nothing on whether I have to sign or not,” he said. The financial pressure is gone for Westwood. He states that he has won £16m in prize money on the tour. “I don’t really have to play golf again, but I still love playing golf so it’s given [me] the option what to do over the next few years,” he added. This financial safety net allows him to wait for the right deal. The Path Forward for a Legend Westwood remains one of the most decorated players in European history. item.title: 5 facts to know about Keisha Lance Bottoms, America’s first black female governor
item.description: By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor Her historic victory in Georgia breaks a century-old political barrier for Black women in the United States. The United States has recorded another milestone in its political history following the election of Keisha Lance Bottoms as Georgia’s governor, making her the first Black woman elected governor of a US state. Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, defeated Republican candidate Rick Jackson in the November 3, 2026 gubernatorial election. Her victory is particularly significant in a country where women and Black Americans have historically faced considerable barriers to political representation. Here are five things to know about the woman making history. She is the first Black woman elected governor of a US state Bottoms has broken a significant racial and gender barrier in American politics. Although several women have previously served as governors, no Black woman had ever been elected to lead a US state before her victory in Georgia. Her election represents a landmark moment for Black women in American public life and expands the history of women’s political representation in the country. She will assume office in January 2027. She is also Georgia’s first female governor Beyond making national history as the first Black woman elected governor, Bottoms will also become the first woman to occupy Georgia’s governorship. Her election marks a departure from the state’s political history, in which men have held the office since Georgia became a state. Interestingly, the United States elected its first female governor more than a century ago. Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming became the first woman to take the oath of office as a state governor on January 5, 1925. Ross was elected in November 1924 following the death of her husband, Governor William B. Ross. She subsequently served until January 1927. The distinction is important: Ross made history as the first woman governor, while Bottoms has now made history as the first Black woman elected to the governorship of a US state. She was previously the Mayor of Atlanta Before her historic gubernatorial victory, Bottoms served as Mayor of Atlanta, Georgia’s capital and one of the most prominent cities in the United States. She held the position from 2018 to 2022, becoming a nationally recognised political figure during her tenure. Her mayoral administration coincided with major national developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the protests following the killing of George Floyd in 2020. Her experience in municipal leadership provided a platform for her subsequent return to national politics. She has experience in the White House Bottoms’ political experience extends beyond local government. Following her tenure as Atlanta’s mayor, she joined the administration of former President Joe Biden as a senior adviser and Director of the White House Office of Public Engagement. item.title: De Miguel funeral set for Thursday as Owono breaks silence
item.description: People gather at Gate 9 of the stadium during an event organised by Tenerife supporters to pay tribute to the player Jesus de Miguel, at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium. CD Tenerife’s Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel died today as a result of a blow sustained during the match against Andorra from goalkeeper Jesus Owono, which caused him to go into cardiac arrest. (is associated with: «De Miguel funeral set for Thursday as Owono breaks silence») Europa Press Canarias/EUROPA PRESS/dpa Footballer Jesús de Miguel is set to be buried on Thursday, Spanish media reported, with his club CD Tenerife planning a memorial service at their stadium on Saturday. De Miguel died on Tuesday after suffering a cardiac arrest during a Spanish second-division match on Monday following a violent collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono. The keeper, who was sent off for the foul near the halfway line, is being investigated by police. The burial will take place in Navahermosa, the family's home municipality in the province of Toledo, broadcaster Cadena SER reported on Wednesday. The family have thanked people for their condolences but, according to the club, have asked fans "to fully respect their privacy at this terrible time." He leaves behind his partner María and their daughter Carla, born in June 2025. The players, coaching staff and club management of Tenerife will attend the funeral. The club will also pay their respects at a service at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium on the Canary Island on Saturday, with all fans invited. The club have declared a six-day mourning period and suspended all activities of their men's, women's and youth teams until the end of the week. 'Hardest days of my life' - Owono The league match against Granada scheduled for Saturday has been postponed. Andorra also requested a postponement of their next match. According to Spanish media, Tenerife's chief prosecutor José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui believes criminal proceedings over the incident on the pitch are very unlikely despite the police investigation. But Owono faces a long ban from the Spanish football federation (RFEF). "These are the hardest days of my life," the 25-year-old said in the statement from his club, his first public comments since the incident. "It is hard for me to find words, and it is very difficult for me to comprehend what has happened. The loss of Jesús pains me infinitely." The Equatorial Guinea international said that many questions still need to be answered and he would face everything that comes his way "with the utmost respect." He added: "But at the moment, I honestly can think of nothing else but Jesús and the pain we are all experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús."

item.title: How landmark Everton compensation prevented Burnley record loss
item.description: Burnley were bought by ALK Capital in December 2020 using loans secured against the club's assets and other external debt [Getty Images] Six years ago, Burnley were considered one of the best-run clubs in the country. The Clarets were debt free, with £41.65m cash in the bank, and enjoying their fifth successive season of Premier League football. Now they sit in the Championship relegation zone, with concerns over debt and the way the Clarets were bought by ALK Capital using loans and the club's own money. Fans have been very concerned about what the future holds - although on Wednesday there was some rare positive news in the club's accounts. BBC Sport takes a closer look at what is going on at Turf Moor. How did ALK Capital buy the club? You may be familiar with the term "leverage buyout" after the Glazer family's purchase of Manchester United in 2005. It effectively means that a purchase is carried out using debt secured on the club's assets, its own bank balance and other loans, rather than the equity of the buyer. In Burnley's case, ALK Capital took out a £65m loan secured against the club's assets, such as Turf Moor , and used £37m from the club's own bank balance. On top of that, Velocity Capital, the holding company, owed Burnley £80.1m - money which was also used to buy the club. The original £65m loan was partially paid off, but then refinanced and extended to reach £105m in the 2024-25 accounts. Interest rates were as high as 12%. On top of that were factored debts, when a club mortgages off future transfer instalments for a one-off payment from the bank. Burnley owed £37m at an interest rate of 12.75%. In total, the football club's borrowings stood at £142.3m, the 10th-highest external debt in English football. Then came the 2025-26 accounts, published today, which painted a different picture. How owners finally paid off £77.7m used to buy Burnley Now, back to that leveraged buyout which has been attracting so much criticism from fans. Last season's accounts contained a big surprise. Remember Velocity Capital, the holding company that owed Burnley £80.1m for the purchase of the club? The accounts revealed £77.7m of that has now been paid to the Clarets. It cleared a large chunk of the debt used to buy the football club and helped to make the latest accounts look healthier. This was needed because, over the past six years, debts related to the leveraged buyout and associated interest payments had increased. Why Everton's £38.1m compensation was so vital for Burnley The £77.7m payment does not mean all Burnley's financial concerns or debts have been resolved. The club still reported a loss for 2025-26 of £9m, compared with £24m-£29m in the previous three seasons. That might seem positive. But this includes the Velocity Capital payment, money for being in the Premier League - and a landmark compensation payout. The Clarets have been paid £38.8m by Everton because of the Toffees' profit and sustainability breach in 2021-22, which was found

item.title: Bears Likely Hold Kyle Monangai Out For Sunday Night Game
item.description: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images Don’t expect Kyle Monangai to line up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this Sunday. The injury timeline just does not work for a Week 9 return. Monangai has missed four straight games with a thumb injury and turf toe issues. The team kept him off the injured reserve list to save a spot, hoping he would be ready within a four-week window. That window has closed. The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs wrote Tuesday that the team is unlikely to rush him back. The Practice Problem Monangai has not returned to practice yet. Biggs noted that rushing a player back after a month of inactivity is risky. “I’m skeptical they would have Monangai back for two practices — max — after missing a month and then add him to the mix Sunday night against the Buccaneers,” Biggs wrote Tuesday. Two days of practice is barely enough to shake off rust. The Bears need him healthy for the long haul, not just for one prime-time game. The smart play is to wait. A return on Nov. 22 against the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field is what Biggs suggests targeting. Short Yardage Struggles The team has won three of their last four games without him, but the offense still feels the gap. Through eight weeks, the league’s No. 2 rushing offense belongs to Chicago. Roschon Johnson and veteran D’Andre Swift have stepped up well. Swift posted a season-low 2.6 yards per carry during the victory against Seattle. That number shows the team misses Monangai’s hard-charging style on short-yardage downs. Johnson is serviceable, but he lacks the same takeover ability. Twice during the first four games, Monangai hit 100 yards. The Bears need that specific skill set for the stretch run. Waiting for the Bye Head coach Ben Johnson has hinted that another back could see more time soon. The team signed Zavier Scott from the practice squad to the 53-man roster. Johnson said, “We’ve had him up for the last three weeks here, and it’s just been a matter of … that trust level.” Scott played strictly on special teams in Week 8. Johnson observed that if the team requires more bodies, “If that continues to be a thing, I think we’re going to need all three backs to play for us.” Keeping Monangai out until after the Week 10 bye makes the most sense. It gives him time to heal while the team relies on the current rotation. The bye week will provide the extra rest needed to get him fully ready for November.

With the NFL trade deadline slowly approaching , there have still been talks surrounding the Indianapolis Colts and whether they’re still looking to move players. After trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, the one name who continues to pop up is Jonathan Taylor . There’s no doubt that teams would love to have him on their team, but the Colts could also be looking for a hefty return. According to ESPN’s Dan Graziano, one of the teams that seems to be willing to make a deal for him is the New York Giants . “The Colts are still asking for a lot for RB Jonathan Taylor and taking the stance that they don’t need to move him,” Graziano wrote. “Unlike the recently traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Taylor is not in the final year of his contract. He’s 27 years old and could absolutely be a part of Indy’s future if someone doesn’t give the Colts the draft capital they’re seeking. I do get the sense, though, that enough teams are interested in Taylor that it’s too soon for the Colts to think about lowering their demands. I would guess he gets traded, and I wouldn’t be at all surprised if it was the Giants who made that move.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Giants have a need at running back, and Taylor would instantly help improve their offense. It also looks like they’ve been trying to add to their defense as well. “They inquired multiple times on Jeffery Simmons but were told no by Tennessee,” Jeremy Fowler wrote. “Another player on the Giants’ radar is Tampa Bay’s Vita Vea. (The Bucs are not expected to move him.) It would be a mild surprise if New York doesn’t walk away with some help up front.” At this point, it looks like the Giants may be one of the busier teams in the league over the next week. item.title: Former Yankee pitcher explains retirement decision: ‘Nothing really materialized’
item.description: Chad Green, a reliable bullpen arm for the Yankees from 2016-22, has confirmed his retirement from MLB. “I officially just called it quits in April, early April,” Green said in an interview with Randy Olson of AreaSports. “I was still throwing and stuff once I got designated last year. I was still kind of working out and throwing and getting ready just in case an offer was worth it and something that I could leave and go do. But nothing really materialized… I really only called it quits in April.” The Toronto Blue Jays designated Green for assignment on July 29, 2025, after acquiring reliever Seranthony Dominguez. The Blue Jays then released Green in August 2025, effectively bringing his career to an end. Green was selected by the Detroit Tigers in the 11th round of the 2013 MLB draft out of Louisville. He was traded to the Yankees in December 2015 and made his major-league debut in 2016. With the Yankees in 2017, Green went 5-0 with a 1.83 ERA and 103 strikeouts over 69 innings. “When you’re going through a year like that, you don’t even realize what’s going on,” Green said. “New York was a place we’re not familiar with. Me and my wife had never been there before, so it’s like what do we do, where do we stay, how do we get to the ballpark, so things are happening so fast and you’re pitching well on top of it, a year like that goes by so fast. “Having success early on definitely helps you set yourself up way better down the line.” MORE BY ADAM ZAGORIA Former Yankees slugger wins U.S. House seat in Texas Nov. 4, 2026, 10:18 a.m. Brewers manager called Brian Cashman after controversial Yankees comments Nov. 4, 2026, 9:13 a.m. He had Tommy John surgery in 2022. “I didn’t finish my Yankee career the way I wanted it, had Tommy John surgery,” he said. “I knew that time was coming to an end, just how they operate, and they don’t sign guys who are hurt. I was going into my free agency year, which was obviously a bad time to get hurt, and then luckily signed with Toronto.” Green finished his major league career with a 3.43 ERA, 43 wins, 29 saves and 591 strikeouts across 492.2 innings. “I have no ill feelings towards baseball,” he said. “We’re definitely grateful for our experience.” Read the original article on NJ.com . item.title: Lee Westwood Calls Himself Unemployed Amid LIV Golf Chaos
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images A former world number one golfer told the world he has no job. Lee Westwood, 53, sat on a podcast and said he is currently unemployed. This is not a joke or a marketing stunt. The English star has signed no contract for the new LIV Golf 2.0 plan. He has also not returned to the DP World Tour. His playing future is a blank slate as of Tuesday. Westwood made these comments on The Chipping Forecast podcast. He stated clearly, “I am currently unemployed.” He added, “I haven’t signed up to anything anywhere. I haven’t made a decision on anything yet.” The situation is unique for a player who joined the Saudi-backed tour in 2022. Now, the league is shifting gears without its original funding source. Several big names like Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia have already walked away. Westwood says nothing has been offered that he likes for the new version. “There’s nothing that’s been presented to me that was agreeable for LIV 2.0,” Westwood said. The Cost of Leaving Westwood faces a hard choice if he wants to play on European soil again. He would need to reapply for membership by November 16. But the price of return is steep. A 10-tournament suspension would block him from competing for months. He explained the timeline on the podcast. “I know that if I sign up on the 12th of November, I’ve then got to serve a 10-tournament suspension, which takes me through the South African Open.” This means his first game back would likely be the Turkish Airlines Open in early May. The financial pressure to stay is gone for Westwood. He earned a fortune during his time on the breakaway tour. Over the past four and a half years, reports show he secured £16m in prize money. He admits he would have been foolish not to take the money when it was offered. “I’ve made a fortune over the last four and a half years,” added Westwood. He says he does not need to play to survive. Yet he still loves the game. This love is why he is waiting for the right offer instead of taking the first one he sees. The LIV 2.0 Problem The new LIV structure lacks the deep pockets it once had. The Saudi Public Investment Fund pulled its backing, leading the league to file for bankruptcy protection last month. A new financing deal of $300m is on the table, but few players have signed up. Jon Rahm told reporters he was not thrilled with the changes for 2.0. He felt the tour was moving away from team golf. Westwood shares this hesitation. He notes that deadlines have passed with no clear direction on signing. Westwood is not the only one stuck in limbo. Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton are also not returning to the new setup. The uncertainty leaves many veterans without a schedule. Westwood says there are still many details that need fine-tuning. “I haven’t signed for 2.0. I haven’t signed anything,” he told GolfMagic . He has heard nothing about whether a signature is even required yet. The silence from the tour is loud. Westwood is watching the clock but will not rush a bad deal.

item.title: Jack Campbell shares ‘optimistic’ update after scary neck injury
item.description: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has shared an “optimistic” update days after suffering a scary neck injury against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell was injured while making a tackle during Sunday’s game against Minnesota, and after laying motionless on the Ford Field turf for an extended period, he was stabilized on a stretcher and taken to a hospital for further evaluation and tests. Updates from the team were rather matter-of-fact, reflecting a desire to respect his and his family’s wishes. On Wednesday, Campbell shared a lengthy update on social media, relaying that he has “full movement” in his lower body, and that he is “continuing to make progress with movement” in his upper body. Campbell also thanked the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded to his injury during the game, as well as the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital. You can read the full statement here : STATEMENT FROM JACK CAMPBELL My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong

item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 01: Quarterback Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts hands off the ball to runningback Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts during the second half of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the November 10 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaching, the Indianapolis Colts are facing one of their most difficult decisions in recent memory: whether to trade superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. Following the departures of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, Indianapolis appears to be embracing a rebuilding approach, and Taylor could be the next major name on his way out. Multiple teams have reportedly expressed interest in acquiring the 27-year-old, including the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks and New York Giants, with the Colts reportedly seeking compensation equivalent to a first-round pick. While Taylor remains one of the NFL’s premier running backs, the question is whether his remaining prime years align with Indianapolis’ timeline for returning to contention. He is under contract through 2028 and has publicly expressed his desire to remain with the franchise, but with the Colts sitting at 2-6 and already without their 2027 first-round selection, acquiring additional premium draft capital could prove extremely valuable. On the other hand, trading Taylor would leave an already struggling offense without its most dependable playmaker, potentially making life even more difficult for whoever eventually takes over at quarterback. With the deadline just days away, should Indianapolis capitalize on Taylor’s trade value or retain him as a cornerstone of its future? Should Jonathan Taylor be traded? Are you confident in the Colts? Any optimism surrounding the Colts following Chris Ballard’s dismissal appears to be fading quickly, particularly after Sunday’s humiliating 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Indianapolis was thoroughly outplayed on both sides of the football, trailing 28-0 at halftime before eventually suffering its fourth consecutive defeat. The offense managed just seven points, while the defense surrendered 42 in a performance that raised further questions about the team’s immediate future under Shane Steichen. What was already shaping up to be a disappointing season has now turned into a potential organizational reset, with several established veterans either traded or reportedly drawing interest from contenders. Last week’s Reacts survey showed that only 31 percent of Colts fans believed the franchise was headed in the right direction, a significant decline from the previous week’s 47 percent. That drop came after the trades of Nelson and Buckner, and the latest defeat is unlikely to have improved the mood surrounding the team.
