item.title: Barcelona held multiple meetings to convince Real Madrid-bound attacking prodigy – report
item.description: Barcelona held multiple meetings to convince Real Madrid-bound attacking prodigy – report One of the biggest transfer stories in recent months was the saga involving JJ Gabriel, Manchester United’s wonderkid. A couple of months ago, it emerged that the English teenager was shopping for a new club, and several European giants, including Barcelona, positioned themselves in the race. However, it has now emerged that Real Madrid have beaten everyone else to the signing of the teenager. Journalist Ben Fernandes Santos has now offered some insight into how much Barcelona wanted to sign Gabriel. The Catalan club considered him one of the biggest talents they had identified in the last decade. Deco is also said to have held several meetings with the player’s camp. Deco made significant efforts to convince JJ Gabriel Santos claims that the Portuguese director was determined to land the 16-year-old, viewing his potential as exceptional. Barcelona tried to convince him that the best next step in his career would be to wear the Blaugrana colours. JJ Gabriel is set to join Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) However, the youngster is said to have had a clear preference throughout the process: his dream was to play for Real Madrid. The Englishman is said to have been very keen on fulfilling that dream, leaving Barcelona fighting a losing battle in trying to convince him. Santos’ claims directly contradict those of Deco, who revealed back in September that the Catalan club were not involved in the race. Barcelona miss out but have enough to be grateful for JJ Gabriel is widely regarded as the single biggest English talent of his generation, and signing him would have been a coup for Barcelona. The Catalan club already have an outstanding young core, and the 16-year-old would have been an excellent addition for the future. However, Barça cannot do much to change a player’s preference. Every footballer has a club he dreams of playing for, and Gabriel dreamt of Real Madrid. Deco doing his best to sign the teenager shows how much the club wanted him, but Barcelona have a lot of their own talents to look after. Barcelona should focus on talents like Ebrima Tunkara. (Picture credit: Instagram/@ebrimatunkara10) Instead of being disappointed that they missed out on the Englishman, the club should focus on the players they have in La Masia . Someone like Ebrima Tunkara, who is the same age as Gabriel, is considered one of the biggest talents in the academy. The 16-year-old completed pre-season with Hansi Flick and has even made matchday squads, coming very close to a first-team debut. Barcelona are fortunate to have an academy that repeatedly produces such talent, and Tunkara will certainly not be the last on the list. The club’s future depends less on winning every transfer battle and more on identifying the next promising talent, and it remains to be seen how Deco goes about it.

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino doubles down on USMNT youth movement as Nations League stakes rise
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino expanded his U.S. player pool earlier this fall by inviting about a dozen young players for a series of friendlies. Most performed so well, they earned callbacks Wednesday — even with most veterans available for the first official matches since the World Cup and a youth-specific Olympic camp taking place at the same time. Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall, Justin Ellis, Mathis Albert, Adri Mehmeti, Neil Pierre and Diego Kochen all parlayed their efforts in September-October into November invitations for the Nations League quarterfinals . Average age: 18.1. “We are playing now an official game [and] the priority always is for the first team,” Pochettino said Wednesday. “And because we all believe that if the players are involved with the first team, [there] is the possibility to keep growing and of course adding more experience — and good experience. It's easy.” The U.S. will begin workouts Monday at the national training center near Atlanta in preparation for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals vs. Haiti. The first leg, or Haitian “home” game, is Nov. 14 in Miami, followed by the decider Nov. 17 in Cincinnati. Pochettino also invited three outsiders: Midfielder Santiago Castañeda, 21, and defender Reed Baker-Whiting, 21, will join their first senior camp and defender Bryan Reynolds, 25, will seek his first appearance for the U.S. since 2023. “Now it's a moment we need to add players to the roster to try to provide a good balance to the team,” Pochettino said of the 2030 World Cup cycle. “It's a great opportunity for different players now, and … to have the possibility to mix younger with experienced players.” Cavan Sullivan is among seven young USMNT prospects who earned another call-up after impressing during the team's four-game winning streak earlier this fall. Taylor Banner/USSF via Getty Images The young influx comes at the expense of seasoned players, such as Tim Weah, Brenden Aaronson, Matt Turner and Joe Scally. In addition, Yunus Musah was passed over after playing in the recent friendlies. The moves also provide cover for experienced players injured or just returning from injury, such as Ricardo Pepi, Haji Wright, Alex Zendejas and Miles Robinson. The veteran core does remain in place: World Cup members Tyler Adams, Malik Tillman, Gio Reyna, Sebastian Berhalter, Chris Richards, Alex Freeman, Antonee Robinson, Sergiño Dest, Auston Trusty and Matt Freese are back in camp after playing in the September-October window. Pochettino also brought back Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie for the first time since the World Cup. The U.S. has advanced to the Nations League’s final four in each of the previous four editions of the regional competition, which doubles as qualifying for next summer’s CONCACAF Gold Cup. item.title: Colts reportedly take unsurprising firm stance in Jonathan Taylor trade talks
item.description: Colts reportedly take unsurprising firm stance in Jonathan Taylor trade talks originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts are trading key pieces from their NFL roster this season to recoup some draft capital as they enter what could be a lengthy multi-year rebuild after firing Chris Ballard. One of the most fascinating players who could be dealt this year is star running back Jonathan Taylor. There's been plenty of buzz about a trade, but so far, the Colts haven't gone for anything. As the deadline nears, doubt might creep in about a trade. ESPN's Dan Graziano revealed that the Colts are taking a stance on the Taylor trade talks that might frustrate other teams, but is perfectly reasonable for the Colts. Instead of simply trading him away, the Colts don't believe they need to trade him this season. Colts take firm stance on Jonathan Taylor trade, might not deal him this season "The Colts are still asking for a lot for RB Jonathan Taylor and taking the stance that they don't need to move him," Graziano writes. This is a noteworthy update for the Colts and the trade market for the star running back. While teams like the Denver Broncos and New York Giants might have serious interest in Taylor, the Colts don't feel like they have to trade him now. He is under contract beyond the 2026 season, so the Colts could keep him for the rest of 2026, aim to get more in a trade next offseason, or even keep him long-term. MORE : Why it's time for Colts to move on from Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones With the Colts already trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, they've made it clear they're selling. But since Taylor isn't hitting free agency after this season, the potential for a trade is a lot less likely than it would be with rentals. Despite so much interest in Taylor this season leading up to the trade deadline, there's a very real possibility that Taylor remains in Indianapolis. This trade saga is far from over, but the current signs are pointing towards the Colts being more than willing to keep Taylor around since he's already under contract beyond 2026. item.title: Houston Astros Face Major Shake-Up After Wild Card Sweep
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The Houston Astros won their division this year, but the victory feels hollow. A historic upset saw the White Sox eliminate them in the opening round. This loss proves that winning the West is not enough when the team cannot beat a lower-seeded opponent. Owner Jim Crane decided that the current path leads nowhere. He fired general manager Dana Brown in August and will not keep manager Joe Espada for next year. A New Leader Takes the Helm Randy Flores has been named the new general manager. He spent years as an assistant general manager and scouting director for the St. Louis Cardinals. Per MLB Trade Rumors , Flores will have a say in hiring the new bench boss for 2027. The organization needs a fresh voice to fix a roster that looks uneven. Although the squad remains competitive, its top talents are aging or approaching free agency. This leadership change signals a shift in how the club approaches the game. Money Tied Up in Aging Stars The financial picture for the Astros is tight and complicated. They have committed $168.35 million just for the 2027 season alone. Total future commitments reach $261.35 million, according to MLB Trade Rumors. Shortstop Carlos Correa holds a massive deal worth $60.5 million through 2028, with the Twins still owing $30 million as part of a trade. First baseman Christian Walker is locked in for $20 million through 2027. Pitcher Josh Hader costs $38 million through 2028. These big contracts limit the team’s ability to sign new talent. They must manage these dollars carefully to stay competitive. Several key players face decisions soon. Tatsuya Imai declined an opt-out after 2026, so he stays for two more years and $36 million. However, he can opt out after 2027. The team also exercised a $13.35 million option on infielder Isaac Paredes. But they declined a $5 million option on pitcher Ryan Weiss, choosing a $500 thousand buyout instead. This mix of options shows a team trying to balance cost and talent. They cannot afford to be too rigid with their money. The Core Fades While Others Rise The trend lines for Houston are moving down. Former stars like Alex Bregman, Justin Verlander, Framber Valdez, and Kyle Tucker are long gone. After capturing 106 wins and a title in 2022, the club posted 90, 88, 87, and 81 victories over the last four seasons. They missed the playoffs entirely in 2025. The 2026 season was a fluke. No other team had previously made the postseason in a complete season with a losing record until they did. That record does not look good on a resume. Free agents like LaMonte Wade Jr., Jake Meyers, and Daulton Varsho will leave soon. The team needs to fill these holes without breaking the bank. The farm system has suffered from penalties related to the sign-stealing scandal. This makes the upcoming years critical for the franchise. If they do not find new talent soon, the window will close completely. The Astros must act fast to rebuild their core before it is too late.

item.title: John Harbaugh Turned The Giants Into NFC East Favorites
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The New York Giants sit in first place in the NFC East, and the shift started with a new coach who refuses to let mistakes slide. John Harbaugh has turned this team around in his first season by demanding total accountability from every player on the roster. Yahoo Sports reports the Giants (4-2-1) are the only team in the division with a winning record as they head into their next matchup. This success comes after the team matched its win total from last year before the season even reached the midway point. Harbaugh did not wait for a crisis to fix the culture. He met with player groups in the locker room immediately after a loss in Los Angeles to stop any self-pity from taking hold. That quick action helped the team bounce back from losing quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season the next morning. Calling Out Traitors to Fix Effort The biggest change is how the staff handles bad effort. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson addressed his unit’s lack of hustle in front of the entire team after a loss to New Orleans. He did not whisper to individuals or hold a side meeting. “You confront it. Just like we do, we confront everything,” Wilson said. He told players he looks at those who do not run to the ball as traitors to the defense. Wilson made it clear that the team will either make adjustments to get those players off the field or wait for them to correct their behavior. Harbaugh and his staff have removed players from the lineup when needed., including Jameis Winston and running back Cam Skattebo. Salary and veteran status mean nothing if the player cannot help the team win. Quarterback Moves That Win Games To secure the strongest opportunity against the Houston Texans, Harbaugh detailed last week’s decision to replace Winston with J.J. McCarthy. Many players found out about the change only when they started reviewing the game plan. There was no grand announcement. The move was met with such nonchalance by Harbaugh that he allowed the facts to speak for themselves. Although Jameis Winston had recorded two wins and a tie across his four starts, the staff determined a change was necessary for that specific week. Harbaugh said of his tactics, “I don’t know if it’s philosophy so much.” He added, “It’s just a week-to-week feel thing with your guys.” The Giants now face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles hold a 2-6 record, but the Giants have not won there since 2013. Harbaugh’s team has been on the field for a final play in five straight games and has lost just once in those tight spots.

item.title: Erin Andrews makes admission about Jack Campbell injury coverage
item.description: NFL sideline reporter Erin Andrews has opened up about the challenges of reporting on serious player injuries, sharing her perspective following Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell’s frightening injury against the Minnesota Vikings. Speaking on the latest episode of Calm Down with Erin and Charissa , the podcast she co-hosts with Charissa Thompson, Andrews discussed the difficult position sideline reporters face when players suffer potentially serious injuries. Andrews admitted that delivering accurate information while respecting the privacy of injured players and their families can be an extremely delicate balancing act. Erin Andrews opens up on the difficulty of reporting Jack Campbell’s injury: ‘You don’t want to misspeak’ https://t.co/C7AV2ZLQfo — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 4, 2026 “You don’t want to misspeak,” Andrews said while discussing the challenges of covering those situations. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Ng-Imagn Images Andrews also explained that her perspective comes from personal experience, having witnessed serious injuries involving her husband, former NHL player Jarret Stoll. She revealed that she had accompanied Stoll in the back of an ambulance on multiple occasions, giving her an understanding of the fear and uncertainty that come with those situations. That experience has helped shape how she approaches injury coverage, particularly when players are receiving medical attention on the field. Andrews acknowledged that sideline reporters are expected to provide updates to a national audience in real time, but obtaining information can be difficult when medical personnel are still evaluating an injured player. “You just want to handle it with as much grace and let the trainers do their gig,” Andrews said. “I felt bad even asking PR, like, ‘Do you have an update?'” MORE: D’Andre Swift passes Walter Payton’s Bears franchise record Jack Campbell’s injury leaves Lions fans concerned Oct 5, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; FOX sideline reporter Erin Andrews interviews Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) after the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. item.title: Bremerton basketball star's final four schools include UW, Gonzaga
item.description: Bremerton High School basketball star Jalen Davis is close to choosing his college destination. Davis, a two-time Class 2A state champion with the Knights, is expected to announce his commitment next week after a visit at Gonzaga University. He's due to return from Spokane Nov. 8. National signing day for Division I basketball recruits is Wednesday, Nov. 11. On Tuesday, Nov. 3, Davis revealed on social media that his final four schools are Gonzaga, Washington, North Carolina and UCLA. He's already made official campus visits with the Huskies, Tar Heels and Bruins. "It's going to be a tough decision truthfully," said Bremerton head coach Miah Davis, Jalen's father. "They all bring great value." Davis, the two-time Kitsap Sun athlete of the year , is ranked as the No. 13 recruit nationally and the No. 1 recruit in the state by 247Sports. As a junior in 2025-26, Davis averaged 30 points, 8.9 rebounds, 5.3 steals and 3.7 assists per game while leading Bremerton to its second consecutive Class 2A state title. He became the Knights' all-time career scorer with 2,064 points and will begin his senior campaign ranked second in West Sound history behind Steven Gray, who scored 2,415 points in his time at Chimacum and Bainbridge before playing collegiately at Gonzaga. Davis is the biggest basketball recruit from Kitsap County since fellow Bremerton alum Marvin Williams, who signed North Carolina in 2003 and led the Tar Heels to the NCAA national title in his only collegiate season before heading to the NBA. Bremerton is scheduled to begin the 2026-27 season Dec. 8 against Port Angeles. Among the Knights' top game this campaign is a Dec. 19 road game against Rainier Beach, the defending 3A state champ. The Vikings' roster features JJ Crawford, one of the top Class of 2029 national recruits. item.title: “It Ain’t Going to Go Well”- Dale Jr. Issues Harsh Reality Check on Dodge’s NASCAR Return
item.description: NASCAR, Motorsport, USA Xfinity Series 2023: Food City 300 NASCAR Xfinity Series Driver Dale Earnhardt Jr. 88 takes to the track for the Food City 300 at the Bristol Motor Speedway in Bristol TN. LicenseRM 20751467 Copyright: xZoonar.com/LoganxTxArcexGrindstonexMediaxGroup/ActionxSportsxPhotographyx 20751467 ©IMAGO/Zoonar Dodge’s return to NASCAR marks a significant moment for the sport, which will once again have four manufacturers competing at the highest level. But while the announcement has generated plenty of excitement, Dale Earnhardt Jr. isn’t expecting the returning brand to have an easy ride when it finally hits the track. “ It ain’t going to go well . It is going to be a struggle,” Dale Earnhardt Jr. said, offering a blunt prediction for Dodge as the manufacturer prepares to return to NASCAR’s Cup Series in 2027. After a 14-year absence, Dodge is finally bringing its muscle back to NASCAR’s premier division. The manufacturer officially confirmed its 2027 Cup Series return at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas, with Kaulig Racing preparing to field two Dodge Charger entries. While the comeback has generated plenty of excitement, the NASCAR Hall of Famer believes the combination of a new OEM and a developing Cup organization could make the initial transition particularly difficult. Dale Jr. isn't holding back on Dodge's ambitious comeback. Subscribe to stay ahead of the biggest shifts reshaping NASCAR's competitive landscape. “They know that, and they’re not ready for it, but they know it’s going to be part of the process. It’s going to be some tough road. It’s going to be a tough road ahead,” he added. Dale Jr. believes Dodge will need considerable time to establish itself against Chevrolet, Ford, and Toyota. He pointed to Toyota’s arrival in the Cup Series in 2007 as an example of why a new manufacturer should not expect immediate success. Toyota entered NASCAR’s premier division with four major organizations: Joe Gibbs Racing, Bill Davis Racing, Michael Waltrip Racing, and Team Red Bull. Despite that backing, its inaugural season produced no victories. Dave Blaney secured Toyota’s first Cup pole at New Hampshire in June 2007, but the manufacturer had to wait until March 2008 for Kyle Busch to deliver its maiden victory at Atlanta Motor Speedway in the No. 18 JGR Toyota. Toyota’s progress came in stages. Kyle Busch won eight races in 2008 overall. However, its first major championship at NASCAR’s top level took longer. Busch secured Toyota’s first Cup Series drivers’ title in 2015, followed by the manufacturer’s first Cup Series championship in 2016. That development curve is precisely what Dale Jr. expects Dodge to experience. He also believes an immediate breakthrough could create an entirely different problem. If a new manufacturer enters such a technically advanced competition and starts winning immediately, established competitors will inevitably question whether it has a competitive advantage. Dodge will need time to develop its equipment

item.title: Toronto FC’s Comeback Streak Finally Snaps In Atlanta
item.description: Jordan Godfree-Imagn Images The magic ran out on Sunday night in Atlanta. For months, Toronto FC found a way to claw back into games, but that resilience hit a hard wall at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The 3-1 loss officially ended the team’s season and their playoff hopes for the sixth straight year. This was not a game they could lose, yet they gave up two early goals that broke their spirit before halftime. Miguel Almiron opened the scoring for the hosts in the 22nd minute. Toronto could not mount a comeback this time. Coach Robin Fraser told reporters that the early mistakes were “soft goals” that changed the entire game. He stated that conceding two goals at the start rendered the remainder of the match desperate. “We’ve been talking about moments all year, and we end up giving up a couple of soft goals, and that changed everything,” Fraser said to reporters, according to Waking The Red . The team simply ran out of time to fix the mess. The Injury Toll and the Hole They Dug Fraser pointed to the first half of the season as a major reason for the struggle. “I do think that the injuries in the first half of the season really hurt us,” Fraser said, according to Yahoo Sports . Those missed players left gaps that Atlanta exploited with ease. A total of 63 goals conceded by Toronto this year, 19 higher than the 2025 figure, reveals the extent of the damage. Finishing 12th with a 9-12-12 record, they reached the final weekend. With no path to close the gap, they remained four points behind the playoff threshold. Even though Lewis Morgan scored a late goal in the 79th minute, it was too little, too late. That was the only shot on target to score for the visitors. Captain Jonathan Osorio knew the group had the talent to make it but fell short. “I’m just very disappointed that we weren’t able to make the playoffs this year with the team that we have,” Osorio said. The fans watched their team fight hard all year, but the defense could not hold the line when it mattered most. History Repeats Itself in Georgia Mercedes-Benz Stadium remains a house of horrors for this squad. Atlanta has not seen a Toronto victory since the 2019 MLS Eastern Conference final match. The pattern of late collapses finally broke, but not in their favor. Comebacks after the 80th minute generated 18 points this season, accounting for almost half their overall tally. You cannot live on hope forever, and this loss proves it. According to reports, the decisive factor was allowing two goals before halftime. The season ends with a trip to Philadelphia on Saturday, November 7. The team faces the Union on MLS Decision Day, but the playoff race is already over for them. “We had some moments that let us down, and when you go down, give up a goal, it changes the game,” Fraser added. The reality is clear. For the sixth consecutive season, Toronto FC will be absent from the postseason. The comeback streak is dead, and the rebuilding starts now.

item.title: Lions' Jack Campbell releases statement on progress of neck injury
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body, according to a statement he released through the team on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Campbell is continuing to make progress following a serious neck injury that forced him to be carted off the field and immediately hospitalized in a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings . "My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express," the statement said. "I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." On the opening play of the fourth quarter in Sunday's win, Campbell went limp on what appeared to be a routine tackle of tight end T.J. Hockenson and received on-field medical attention for several minutes before being carted off on a stretcher and taken immediately to a local hospital. "My faith in God has never been stronger," Campbell's statement continued. "I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. "I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. "I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. "To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. "One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. "Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. "God is good. My faith is strong." The statement is the first we've heard from Campbell since the injury. The Lions released a statement at 7:08 p.m. on Sunday that Campbell was resting and would remain at the hospital for continued evaluation and monitoring

item.title: New Report Opens Door For NY Knicks & Mitchell Robinson Reunion Later This Season
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A new report just opened the door to an unexpected reunion between the New York Knicks and Mitchell Robinson later this season. This was a productive offseason for the Knicks, for the most part. While they celebrated the franchise’s first championship in over five decades, the front office was able to agree to new deals with Landry Shamet, Jose Alvarado, and Jordan Clarkson to keep their championship team intact. However, there was one notable departure in the summer. With Knicks owner James Dolan unwilling to go over the second salary tax apron, New York lost the fan-favorite big man to rivals, the Boston Celtics , in free agency. While his numbers have never jumped off the page, supporters of the team knew how valuable he was in their journey to being champions. Most assumed the Celtics understood that as well, and that is why they gave him a three-year deal worth $47.3 million . However, Robinson has not made quite the impact some expected in Boston, as Heavy’s Sean Deveney perfectly explained on Wednesday. “It’s been a rough start in Boston for new Celtics center Mitchell Robinson, whose offensive rebounding superpower has been removed from his arsenal as the Celtics have tried to allow him to showcase a wider offensive range,” he wrote. “As coach Joe Mazzulla noted, that means Robinson is farther from the basket, and in the process, he has gone from a guy who averaged 4.2 offensive rebounds last year to 1.8 this year.” A New York Knicks and Mitchell Robinson reunion in January may be a real possibility Oct 23, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns (32) celebrates next to Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson (4) after making a three point basket during the second quarter at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Robinson is, arguably, the best offensive rebounder on the planet. It is a special skill not every big man has. But if he is not dominating on the offensive glass, he does not have the same value. It is why the NBA insider speculated, “If this looks to be a bad fit when late January comes around, it is fair to wonder whether the Celtics might get Robinson onto the [trade] market sooner rather than later.” While there will surely be others interested in Robinson’s unique skill set, no team knows him better, or how best to use him, than the Knicks. If New York continues to have their struggles offensively, especially on the offensive boards, the front office would be silly not to check in about a potential trade. Yes, a deal might take them over the second apron, but they can figure out how to get back under — a contract extension with Karl-Anthony Towns, perhaps — in the offseason. Furthermore, while some teams may think the Celtics would be against trading Robinson back to the Knicks, let’s not forget, this is the same team that traded Jaylen Brown to the same team that eliminated them in the playoffs this spring. item.title: 2027: Atiku Vows To Tackle Insecurity At Sokoto Campaign Flag-Off, Says Nothing Will Stop ADC
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, declaring that alleged attempts to frustrate his party’s campaign will not stop its activities ahead of the 2027 general election. Atiku spoke on Wednesday at the flag-off of his presidential campaign in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the ADC and vote for the party in the forthcoming election. His declaration came a day after he accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of plotting to disrupt the campaign rally, alleging that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. At a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, the former Vice President also accused the state government of denying the ADC access to public facilities and logistical support for the rally. He described the alleged restrictions as deliberate attempts to deny the opposition party a level playing field. The DSS subsequently ordered an investigation into Atiku’s allegation, saying the directive was issued by its Director-General despite the Service describing the claim as inconsistent with its operations. In its response, the agency said its operatives had provided security protection to political actors across party lines. It cited an incident involving the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, whom its personnel reportedly evacuated to safety after he was attacked on October 31. Despite the controversy, Atiku proceeded with the campaign flag-off, saying no attempt to frustrate the party would deter it from addressing the people of Sokoto. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. He explained that the state was deliberately chosen for the campaign launch because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. The ADC candidate recalled the promises he made during his previous campaign, saying he had returned to reaffirm his commitment to those pledges, particularly his promise to tackle insecurity if elected president. He also called on Nigerians to turn out in large numbers on election day and vote for the ADC, expressing confidence in the party’s political mission. The rally marks the formal commencement of Atiku’s presidential campaign activities in Sokoto ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: Oborevwori assures residents of peaceful elections
item.description: Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta has assured residents of the state of peaceful, free and fair elections. He also warned political parties against violence and urged all to respect the rule of law. Oborevwori gave the assurance at a stakeholders’ meeting on electoral security on Wednesday in Asaba. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the meeting is organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Represented by his Senior Political Adviser, Sen. Emmanuel Aguariavwodo, Oborevwori reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing a conducive political environment for all parties. According to him, all political parties are free to campaign and canvass for votes without intimidation or harassment. The governor also urged political parties to sell their programmes and ideas to the electorate through peaceful campaigns and other lawful engagements. He however, warned that anyone who violated the law would face the consequences, irrespective of political affiliation. Oborevwori while pledging the state government’s support for INEC and its Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, noted that achieving credible elections required collective commitment from all. According to him, this include from the INEC, security agencies, political parties, civil society organisations and the electorate,” he said. He added that no single institution could deliver credible elections independently, urging all stakeholders to collaborate in preventing electoral violence. Also speaking, the state Commissioner of Police, Mr Samuel Erale, warned political parties and their supporters against violence, declaring that security agencies were fully prepared to enforce electoral laws. Erale said that the police would monitor political activities and maintain peace before, during and after the elections. “We want to be peaceful. We will be on ground. We will monitor all the activities of everyone,” he said. The CP said security agencies would provide a level playing field for all political parties to exercise their democratic rights within the provisions of the law. He warned that anyone who resorted to violence or breached electoral regulations would face the full weight of the law. “The moment violence is involved, you leave us with no choice than to come and do our duties,” he said. He stressed that maintaining peace, providing a level playing field and ensuring compliance with electoral laws were key priorities of security agencies. He added that no individual, political party or contestant would be exempted from enforcement of electoral laws. Erale also assured stakeholders that security agencies would not compromise their responsibilities, stressing their commitment to credible and transparent elections. He urged political stakeholders to cooperate with security agencies to ensure peaceful campaigns and a violence-free electoral process. item.title: Bare metal boom: On-prem server sales for HPC and AI up 20% this year
item.description: On-premises high-performance compute (HPC) is still in demand, according to Hyperion Research, which estimates the market is expanding at almost 20 percent year-on-year, often driven by requirements for AI processing. What Hyperion calls the "on-premises HPC and AI-for-Science" server market showed significant growth in the first half of 2026, with revenues hitting $16.5 billion, up 19.9 percent. However, the analyst says unit shipments over the same period grew only 4.4 percent, meaning that systems are carrying a higher price tag due to greater use of costly components such as GPUs and other accelerators, not to mention the effects of higher memory costs, which have tripled or quadrupled since last year. Its tracking of the HPC market is based on multiple surveys conducted of both buyers and suppliers, the firm says. The latest data shows a major change in the overall HPC market growth, heavily driven by a combination of the use of AI, large language models (LLMs), and purchases of large GPU/accelerator-based systems. This trend was noted a couple of years ago, with Omdia reporting in 2024 that revenue growth from server sales was racing ahead of actual units shipped, as customers prioritized investment in highly configured server clusters for AI . Much of that spending was by hyperscalers and cloud providers, seeking to profit from selling AI services to enterprise customers, but Hyperion’s figures focus on on-prem shipments, showing that many enterprises prefer to do their processing in-house. According to Hyperion, Dell has now surpassed HPE as the biggest HPC vendor, with server revenues of $4.2 billion for the first half of 2026. HPE, which picked up supercomputing specialist Cray for $1.3 billion in 2019, had long been pack leader in the global HPC arena in terms of market share and revenue. The figures put Dell on a 24 percent share, while HPE is not far behind on 21 percent. Lenovo and China-based Sugon trail behind at 4 percent share each, while 45 percent of the market is just labelled as "others" by Hyperion. This includes names such as Bull, which re-emerged from the shadows of Atos this year, plus Supermicro, Penguin Computing, and NEC. The HPC infrastructure market is inherently cyclical. HPE recognized significant revenue in 2025 with sales of multiple exascale-class leadership machines, but procurement of that scale is intermittent and doesn't necessarily come along every year, Hyperion notes. "Organizations and institutions are continuing to invest in their advanced computing infrastructure due to both replacing aging machines and the desire to adopt AI into their workflows to support their businesses and missions," said Hyperion Research CEO Earl Joseph. "The growth reflects both a nominal increase in units being purchased and significant increases in system prices." HPC systems are considered the backbone for many AI and AI-related applications, which has driven the overall HPC market to a new growth level, Joseph added. ®

item.title: Afenifere, Igbo forum seek stronger Yoruba-Igbo ties, back Tinubu, Hamzat
item.description: The Afenifere and Ndi Igbo Unity Forum have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening Yoruba-Igbo relations and promoting peaceful coexistence in Lagos State. Chief ​‌‍‍‍‍Deji Wellington, State Chairman of Afenifere, a Yoruba socio-cultural organisation, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, after a meeting with leaders of the Igbo community aimed at rebuilding cordial relationships between the two ethnic groups. Wellington said the initiative was designed to change the existing narrative and restore the cordial relationship that previously existed between the Yoruba and Igbo communities. He said it was important for Igbo residents to regard Lagos as their home and maintain peaceful relationships with their host community. “It is our desire that the Ndi Igbo (Igbo people) see Lagos as home, where they are expected to work peacefully with the host community. “They should establish good relationships with the Lagos State Government and subsequently protect their businesses, investments and properties,” he said. Wellington said stronger relationships between the Igbo community, the host community and the state government would promote mutual understanding, security and peaceful coexistence. He said the initiative was also aimed at creating an atmosphere where residents from both ethnic groups could pursue their economic interests without fear or hostility. Wellington said Igbo leaders had pledged their support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition and the 2027 governorship aspiration of Lagos State Deputy Governor and APC candidate Dr Obafemi Hamzat. He said the forum also promised to collaborate in mobilising support for Tinubu and Hamzat across the state. Wellington said the forum pledged to take the campaign to local government areas, wards and Igbo communities across the state. “The Igbo leaders have promised to join Afenifere in its determination to rally support for the President’s second term and Dr Hamzat as Lagos State Governor in the 2027 election,” Wellington said. He expressed optimism that the partnership would strengthen inter-ethnic relations, deepen political cooperation and promote a more peaceful and inclusive environment in the state. item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Labour veterans from the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have intervened in the face-off between the President of the NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo. The two labour leaders have recently traded words over the recent approval of ₦70,000 by the Federal Government to cushion the effect of high transportation costs occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy. The rift between the two leaders degenerated into personal attacks on national television, a situation that has affected unity within the labour sector. Worried by the development, labour veterans met to bring the situation under control. Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), Comrade Wabba said the labour veterans had been able to arrest any form of hostility between the two leaders. The former NLC President told journalists that veterans from the two labour centres had met to resolve what he described as a family misunderstanding between the two centres. He said the veterans emphasised that workers’ organisations must remain united because they share a single objective and aim. The former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) said all hostilities had been ordered to stop, explaining that the goal is to prevent future occurrences through formal dialogue. He said: “It’s a family misunderstanding between the two centres, and we have made it clear that workers’ organisations are supposed to be one because the objective is one and the aim is one. “So, that seeming misunderstanding has escalated, and we have said all hostilities should stop. We will actually try to meet with them to see what happened and how future occurrences can also be prevented. “So, basically, I can tell you for sure that veterans from both sides—TUC and NLC—namely Peter Esele, Bobboi Kaigama, Hassan Sunmonu, Abdulwaheed Omar, and my humble self, actually met and tried to look at the issue. We said we would meet formally when all of them are available because we just communicated among ourselves, the veterans, and we communicated with them, and they mutually accepted. “The TUC General Secretary was here; I was here; the NLC President was here. All of us embraced ourselves and said, ‘Well, it’s a family issue.’ Therefore, we have also said members of the press should not actually try to advance issues that are not there because, even in your immediate family, you can have some internal issues. “But that internal issue is certainly meant to be resolved, and we are working towards that very effectively because that is the hallmark of trade unionism: to resolve issues, even with our employers, through dialogue and social dialogue. So, basically, it is an issue we have practised, and therefore we will try to now put it into action.” The former NLC President said some of the protagonists i

item.title: VMware returns to low-end server virtualization with 'vSphere Express'
item.description: As first reported by The Register , VMware has returned to the low-end server virtualization market with a product called "vSphere Express." The product will run on up to 128 processor cores and includes vMotion to allow live migration of VMs, automated restart of failed VMs, a distributed switch, rapid non-disruptive patching, and support for physical and virtual trusted platform modules. "We have been listening to the market at the low end, and they want a basic core server virtualization platform," said Prashanth Shenoy, vice president of product marketing in Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF). He explained that each instance of vSphere Express will be discrete, meaning it won't be possible to manage them centrally. "This is tested for small implementations," he told The Register . "We do not want a customer to run this on thousands of cores." Shenoy said the vSphere Foundation (VVF) enterprise virtualization product, and Cloud Foundation (VCF) private cloud suite, are appropriate for users with more complex needs. vSphere Express will, however, match the release cadence of VVF and VCF. Under Broadcom’s ownership, VMware has enormously reduced the number of resellers in its channel program , meaning it no longer has partners who are a good fit for this product. The virtualization giant will therefore sell vSphere Express through its distributors, most of which now operate cloud marketplaces at which affiliated resellers can acquire software – an arrangement channel folk call "two tier distribution." We asked VMware to tell us the price it will charge for vSphere Express. A spokesperson told us it will offer a per-core subscription license at a price "significantly lower" than VVF or VCF but declined to quote a dollar amount. "We encourage interested customers to reach out to their local reseller for information related to pricing and subscription terms," the spokesperson wrote. VMware has also bulked out VVF and VCF a little, by adding disaster recovery and policy-based networking for virtual private clouds that it previously sold as add-ons. Shenoy pitched the additions as demonstrating VMware's intention to add value to VVF and VCF, in part by ensuring the bundles include tools that users are likely to consider represent essential functionality. The Broadcom business unit will also add new features, such as native AWS S3-compatible object storage for its VSAN virtual storage. That update, due in calendar Q1 of 2027, means VSAN will become a more convenient platform on which to store the unstructured data that AI workloads rely on, therefore boosting the utility of VMware's AI Factory. VMware also plans to make its AI Factory easier to implement. "The idea is to focus more on AI, less on setup," Shenoy said. Analysis: A welcome low-end return faces an uncertain reception VMware's return to the low-end server virtualization market may not be well-received, because it has largely ignored users of its existing low-end vSphere Standard prod

item.title: NASA's Artemis II moon launch tore a hole in Earth's upper atmosphere so huge it disrupted GPS signals
item.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

The launch of NASA's Artemis II mission in April 2026 caused significant disturbances in Earth's ionosphere that could have triggered temporary, localized errors in GPS positioning, a new study has found. The study, by a team of researchers from National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan, analyzed data from high-precision networks of fixed, ground-based GPS receivers, used by U.S. scientific institutions to measure the minuscule motions of Earth's tectonic plates in the lead-up to earthquakes. By measuring how long it takes GPS signals to travel from space to ground stations, the researchers were able to reconstruct how the passage of the Artemis II mission's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket changed the concentrations of free electrons in the ionosphere — the electrically charged layer of Earth's atmosphere at altitudes above 30 miles (50 kilometers). The measurements found that the ionospheric disturbances resulting from the sheer power of the Artemis II launch were more significant than any caused by other rocket launches to date and up to ten times more intense than those observed following the test launches of SpaceX's Starship , which is twice as powerful as the SLS based on liftoff thrust. Artemis II saw humans return to the lunar space for the first time in more than fifty years, a mission that NASA hopes will pave the way for lunar landings and eventually the establishment of a sustained human presence on the moon . During the mission's launch, ground-based GPS stations detected changes in the ionospheric electron density equivalent to positioning errors of several meters. Such inaccuracies could easily throw self-driving cars off track, potentially causing traffic collisions, according to Charles Lin, an earth science professor at National Cheng Kung University and one of the co-authors of the paper. "A positioning error of a couple of meters is enough to cause an autonomous car to change lanes," Lin told Space.com. "It could have a strong impact not only on self-driving cars but also on drone positioning." item.title: NNPC posts N3.49trn profit in nine months
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja ABUJA — The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) recorded a cumulative Profit After Tax (PAT) of N3.494 trillion between January and September 2026, following an 18.1 per cent increase in its September profit to N509 billion. The September profit rose from N431 billion recorded in August, according to the company’s September 2026 Monthly Operations and Financial Report. The latest figures bring NNPC’s cumulative profit for the first nine months of 2026 to N3.494 trillion. A breakdown of the performance showed that the company recorded profits of N385 billion in January, N136 billion in February, N276 billion in March, N481 billion in April, N462 billion in May, N535 billion in June, N279 billion in July, N431 billion in August and N509 billion in September. The report also showed that NNPC generated N33.152 trillion in revenue during the nine-month period. Its September revenue stood at N4.608 trillion, representing a 23.3 per cent increase from the N3.737 trillion recorded in August. Monthly revenue figures showed that the company generated N2.571 trillion in January, N2.680 trillion in February, N2.774 trillion in March, N4.971 trillion in April, N4.335 trillion in May, N4.389 trillion in June and N3.087 trillion in July. On its statutory obligations, NNPC disclosed that payments to the Federation Account and other statutory remittances rose to N11.14 trillion between January and September. The amount represents an increase of 17.4 per cent, or N1.65 trillion, over the N9.49 trillion recorded between January and August. On the operational front, average crude oil and condensate production stood at 1.70 million barrels per day in September. Natural gas production also increased to 7,789 million standard cubic feet per day, compared with 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day recorded in August. Total hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil, condensate and natural gas equivalent, averaged 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day during the period. The company further reported 100 per cent availability of its upstream pipeline infrastructure in September. On gas infrastructure projects, NNPC said the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) Gas Pipeline had achieved 100 per cent completion, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline was 95 per cent complete. It added that the OB3 River Niger Crossing pipeline had been commissioned and operationalised. According to the company, collaboration with relevant stakeholders was ongoing to accelerate construction and pre-commissioning activities on the AKK project, with a target of delivering early gas supply to Abuja before the end of 2026. The post NNPC posts N3.49trn profit in nine months appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders, reduce pilgrimage costs
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore petroleum subsidy, tackle insecurity, reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries and reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful if elected president in 2027. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the pledges on Wednesday during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he outlined his proposed measures to address the country’s economic challenges, insecurity and declining standard of living. He said his administration would prioritise the welfare of Nigerians, adding that restoring petroleum subsidy would be among the measures considered to ease the burden of rising fuel prices and reduce transportation costs and the prices of essential commodities. The former vice-president also promised to take decisive steps to address insecurity across the country, protect lives and property and restore confidence in the nation’s security architecture. He said Nigerians deserved to live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. On the economy, Atiku pledged to reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries to revive economic activities, strengthen regional trade and improve the livelihoods of communities dependent on cross-border commerce. He said the move would create opportunities for traders, farmers and other economic operators while strengthening Nigeria’s commercial relations with neighbouring countries. The ADC candidate also promised to reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful, arguing that the cost of religious journeys should not constitute an overwhelming burden for ordinary Nigerians. He said his proposed administration would introduce policies to improve citizens’ welfare, expand economic opportunities and address the hardship confronting households. Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 presidential election, saying the party would provide an alternative direction for the country. Senator David Mark speaks Speaking at the rally, the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, said the reception he witnessed from the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport to Sokoto metropolis indicated widespread support for the party in the state. He expressed confidence that the people of Sokoto would vote for Atiku and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections. Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal speaks Also addressing the gathering, former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration, accusing it of worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country. Tambuwal said the ruling party had failed to provide the leadership required to address Nigeria’s economic and security challenges. item.title: NASA Navigation Experiment Shows Promise for Planetary Landings
item.description: 3 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) An Alta-X drone flies an advanced guidance and navigation system known as the Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) experiment near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, on Wednesday, July 15, 2026. Researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston developed SPLICE, which successfully communicated with the remotely piloted aircraft during hover maneuvers in flight. SPLICE will help spacecraft land precisely and detect and avoid potential hazards, which is critical for NASA missions to the Moon and to Mars. NASA/Ryan Kline NASA successfully demonstrated technology designed to help spacecraft autonomously navigate to safe landing sites on the Moon and on other planets. An Alta-X drone equipped with the agency’s Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution ( SPLICE ) guidance, navigation, and control payload completed simulated lunar descent and landing maneuvers Aug. 27. The flight took place at Rogers Dry Lake near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. During the tests, the SPLICE payload used an advanced guidance system to map the terrain and assess potential landing areas. If the system determines the targeted landing area is unsafe, the system diverts the drone to a safer location. The system generates high-resolution digital elevation maps from light-detection and sensor data. Davis Adams, project manager, confirms that an advanced guidance and navigation system known as the Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) experiment is communicating with an Alta-X drone near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, on Wednesday, July 15, 2026. Researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston developed SPLICE, which successfully communicated with the remotely piloted aircraft during hover maneuvers in flight. SPLICE will help spacecraft land precisely and detect and avoid potential hazards, which is critical for NASA missions to the Moon and to Mars. NASA/Ryan Kline Researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston developed the SPLICE payload and partnered with specialists at NASA Armstrong to integrate, test, and fly it aboard the Alta-X drone in June and July. Those tests verified communications, data handling, telemetry, and command- control performance between the SPLICE payload and the drone to prepare for a full-scale test at Voyager Technologies in Mojave, California, later this month. “This flight test is the culmination of almost a decade of work, for the SPLICE project,” said Davis Adams, NASA project manager. “This flight raised the technology readiness level, priming it for integration into future robotic and crewed lunar flights. Validation of the guidance and navigation systems are applicable to terrestrial, lunar, and Martian descent and landing missions.” NASA has worked with a number of commer

item.title: Oyebanji warns commissioners against arrogance, corruption
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has warned newly inaugurated commissioners and special advisers against arrogance, indiscipline, corruption and abuse of office, declaring that his administration would not tolerate unethical conduct or inefficiency. He charged the appointees to remain humble, accountable and committed to delivering quality service to the people, warning that bureaucratic delays and careless mistakes capable of undermining the state’s development agenda would not be condoned. Oyebanji gave the warning on Wednesday in Ado-Ekiti during the inauguration of three commissioners and 10 special advisers into the State Executive Council. The new commissioners are Dayo Apata, SAN, Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance; and Dr Oyebanji Filani, Commissioner for Health and Human Services. The 10 special advisers are Prof. James Olaleye, e-GIS, Lands and Survey; James Folorunso, Bureau of Public Procurement; Dr John Moyo Ekundayo, Office of Transformation, Strategy and Delivery; Bunmi Talabi, Bureau of Special Projects; and Olayinka Oyebode, Chief Press Secretary and Special Adviser on Media. Others are Princess Adetoun Agboola, Special Education and Social Inclusion; Dr Gbenga Oyewole, Development Planning and Budget; Kayode Adaramodu, Economic Affairs and Private Sector Development; Ebenezer Boluwade, Agriculture and Food Security; and Prof. Akeem Azeez, Special Duties. The governor said the inauguration, coming barely two weeks after the swearing-in of the Secretary to the State Government and other key officials, was aimed at ensuring that his second-term administration commenced without delay. He said the second term was not an opportunity for complacency or self-indulgence but a period to consolidate the achievements of the first term and accelerate the state’s development. Oyebanji particularly cautioned returning commissioners against allowing their experience and length of service to create a false sense of indispensability. “I would also like to counsel you to resist the temptation of the illusion of invincibility and indispensability, which could ultimately breed arrogance. At the end of the day, only God is truly indispensable. “We must all therefore remain gracious and wholeheartedly dedicated to our unwavering service to the good people of Ekiti State,” he said. He declared that he would be impatient and intolerant of indiscipline, unethical behaviour and corruption, insisting that all government activities must reflect professionalism, transparency, technical competence and efficiency. Identifying discipline and speed as the two principles that would drive his administration, the governor urged the appointees to ensure that policies and projects were implemented promptly and in accordance with global best practices. “We must work very hard to successfully translate all electoral promises into visible, concrete and life-changing outcomes fo

item.title: Senate advances Agricultural Revolution Bill
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — A bill seeking to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the transformation and modernisation of Nigeria’s agricultural sector has scaled second reading in the Senate. The bill, sponsored by the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), seeks to promote food security, agricultural productivity, mechanisation, irrigation, agricultural financing, agro-industrialisation, rural development and climate-resilient farming. Following its passage at second reading, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, referred the proposed legislation to the Senate Committees on Agricultural Production, Services and Rural Development, and Agricultural Colleges and Institutions for further legislative consideration. Akpabio directed the committees to report back to the Senate within four weeks. The bill, titled, A Bill for an Act to Provide a Comprehensive Legal Framework for the Transformation and Modernisation of Agriculture in Nigeria, is also designed to promote sustainable agricultural development and address longstanding challenges in the sector. Leading the debate on its general principles, Barau lamented that agriculture, which was once the mainstay of Nigeria’s economy, was no longer performing optimally. He recalled that between the 1950s and early 1980s, agricultural production supported numerous industries, including textile and processing companies in Lagos, Kano and Port Harcourt. He regretted that several industries, particularly those in Kano’s Sharada and Bompai industrial areas, which once supported vibrant economic activities, had become largely dormant. Barau also recalled that the Second Republic government introduced the Green Revolution Programme but noted that its implementation lacked an enabling legal framework. According to him, the absence of legislation made it difficult to sustain the programme beyond the administration that introduced it. He said Nigeria had the human and natural resources required to transform agriculture but lacked effective mechanisms to harness the sector’s enormous potential. “The bill is to provoke conversation, bring in our expertise to look at the entire scenario and see how we can change the trajectory,” he said. Barau urged senators to consider the proposed legislation from the perspective of patriotism rather than partisan politics, stressing the need for collective action to reposition the agricultural sector. Contributing, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Monguno (APC, Borno North), said the bill would translate Nigeria’s economic diversification policy from oil dependence to agriculture into practical reality. He said agriculture contributed about 40 per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product and provided approximately 70 per cent of employment. Monguno, however, lamented that Nigeria had consistently fallen short of agricultural budgetary allocation targets, with its highest allocation in recent years standing at approximately five

item.title: 2027: Otti wave enough to secure re-election — Abia LP
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has dismissed suggestions that the growing political influence of former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, could threaten Governor Alex Otti’s re-election chances in 2027, insisting that the governor enjoys sufficient grassroots support to secure another term. The party said the political momentum behind Otti, which it described as the “Otti wave”, was strong enough to withstand opposition and guarantee victory for the Labour Party in the state. There have been suggestions that Obi’s popularity and influence played a significant role in Otti’s victory in the 2023 governorship election and could again determine the outcome of the 2027 poll. However, the Publicity Secretary of the Labour Party in Abia, Chief Emenike Iroegbu, said the party had established a strong grassroots presence across markets, motor parks, local government areas and wards, making it confident of winning all elective positions in the state. Speaking in Umuahia, Iroegbu acknowledged Obi’s political stature but maintained that his influence would not undermine the Labour Party’s position in Abia. He noted that Otti had remained in the Labour Party while the party continued to strengthen its political structures across the state’s 184 wards and 17 local government areas. “What is currently driving political support for the Labour Party in Abia is the ‘Otti wave’. The ‘Otti wave’ is strong enough to withstand any opposition ahead of the 2027 polls. This is the ‘Otti wave’ that has been spreading like wildfire in the 17 LGAs of Abia State,” he said. Iroegbu claimed that candidates of other political parties, including the National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), had been associating themselves with Otti’s popularity through campaign posters and social media posts. He added that the influence of the former Anambra governor was not strong enough to weaken the Labour Party’s political base in Abia. The party spokesman also expressed confidence that its grassroots structures would translate into electoral victories across the state in 2027. On the inclusion of politicians who served in previous administrations in the party’s campaign structures, Iroegbu defended the move, saying political parties should remain open to individuals willing to join and contribute to governance. He argued that admitting such politicians into the Labour Party did not represent a departure from the principles and policies of the Otti administration, insisting that the governor remained firmly in control of his government. The post 2027: Otti wave enough to secure re-election — Abia LP appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NMDPRA warns of risks from Ogun illegal refinery
item.description: …EFCC traces discovery to whistleblower’s tip, surveillance By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has warned that products from an illegal refinery uncovered in Ogere-Remo, Ikenne Local Government Area of Ogun State, could pose serious risks to vehicles, automobile engines and public safety. The authority gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the facility jointly conducted with operatives of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The Ogun State Coordinator of NMDPRA, Dr Atilola Akinyemi, said the facility, which occupies more than three hectares of land, had no operating licence or permit from any regulatory agency and was operating outside the supervision of relevant authorities. He disclosed that the facility had an underground storage tank with an estimated capacity of more than 90,000 litres. Akinyemi described the installation as a crude and illegal operation, saying its structures and equipment appeared designed to replicate the processes of a conventional refinery without complying with the required regulatory, technical and safety standards. “The facility you see here is very crude and completely illegal. This is not a refinery by any standard. This facility does not have a permit from any regulatory authority, and its operations are unknown to the relevant authorities,” he said. He explained that intelligence gathering by the EFCC was instrumental to the discovery, noting that routine regulatory monitoring alone might not have exposed an operation of such magnitude. “This kind of discovery cannot be made through ordinary monitoring alone; it requires intelligence gathering. As the Zonal Director of the EFCC has explained, intelligence was instrumental in uncovering this operation. We need more of such efforts,” he said. According to him, preliminary investigations showed that the facility had designated sections for receiving feedstock, storage, heating, processing and cooling. Other installations discovered during the inspection included underground heating systems, water hydrants for cooling, locally fabricated storage tanks, separation silos and other equipment used in petroleum processing. Akinyemi likened the operation to illegal refining activities that characterised parts of the Niger Delta in the 1990s and early 2000s, questioning the source of the crude materials allegedly being processed at the facility. “One question that comes to mind is: where do they source their feedstock?” he queried. He said the equipment and general layout suggested that the operators had some technical knowledge but had established the facility outside the country’s petroleum regulatory framework. The NMDPRA coordinator cautioned against identifying the recovered products as diesel or Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) based solely on their physical appearance. He said laboratory analysis was necessary to determine their chemical composition and establish whether t

item.title: UNICEF raises polio alert in Niger, detects five cases
item.description: ….Three human infections, two environmental samples identified in Bida, Chanchaga By Clare Nnabuike, Minna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised the alarm over the detection of five polio cases in Niger State, urging residents to intensify surveillance and ensure that children receive routine immunisation against the disease. The five detections comprised three cases identified through human samples and two through environmental surveillance in Bida and Chanchaga Local Government Areas of the state. UNICEF called on residents, parents and community leaders to support vaccination campaigns and sensitisation efforts to prevent further spread of the virus and achieve a polio-free environment. The agency raised the alarm on Wednesday during a mass mobilisation dialogue organised in collaboration with the Niger State Primary Health Care Development Agency. Speaking at the event in Minna, UNICEF’s representative in Niger State, Mrs Grace Odeyemi, urged residents to strengthen disease surveillance and community engagement, particularly in the affected local government areas. She stressed the need for parents to ensure that their children received polio vaccines, describing immunisation as essential to preventing the disease. Odeyemi explained that health officials routinely monitored children with paralysis or symptoms resembling those of polio victims, collecting samples for laboratory testing to establish the actual cause. She said surveillance also involved environmental sampling to detect the virus even when no infected individual had been identified. “We still carry out routine immunisation of the population. We are vaccinating the children to ensure that we eradicate the disease from the state. “We sample humans, that is, any child that we find in the community with paralysis, having a similar feature of polio-affected victims. “We quickly notify our local surveillance officers to collect samples for tests to see if it is polio or something else that is actually causing the paralysis because it’s not only polio virus that causes paralysis,” she said. She disclosed that the virus had been detected through both human and environmental surveillance in Chanchaga and Bida, bringing the total detections in the state to five. The Niger State Immunisation Officer, Abubakar Usman, said routine and emergency vaccination exercises had been intensified to protect children in the affected communities. He disclosed that reactive vaccination had been conducted in areas where the virus was detected to prevent further transmission. Usman said the agency had also embarked on community engagement involving traditional leaders and other intervention groups to educate residents on the dangers of rejecting immunisation. He attributed the detections largely to poor routine immunisation coverage and non-compliance by some parents and caregivers. “The virus was detected in the state.
