item.title: Soludo has awarded 908km of roads since 2022 — Commissioner
item.description: …Ezeobi says 442km asphalted, less than 5km affected by failures By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has awarded contracts for the construction of 908.44 kilometres of roads across the state since Governor Chukwuma Soludo assumed office in 2022, the Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, has said. Ezeobi, who disclosed this while addressing journalists in Awka, said 442 kilometres of the roads had been fully asphalted, describing the administration’s road construction programme as unprecedented in the state’s history. He claimed that the combined road construction achievements of the three previous governors fell short of the number of kilometres asphalted by the Soludo administration. According to him, the government has awarded 143 road contracts since taking office. Addressing complaints on social media about the condition of some roads constructed by the administration, the commissioner said the affected portions amounted to less than five kilometres out of the 442 kilometres asphalted. “Of all the 442 kilometres of road we have asphalted, if you cut the portions that failed as a result of the effects of underground water, they are not up to five kilometres. That means that we have over 95 per cent of all the roads constructed by this administration in perfect condition,” he said. Ezeobi attributed some of the reported road failures to underground water, unusually heavy rainfall and blocked drainage channels, insisting that the government was addressing the affected sections. He alleged that some residents deliberately blocked drainage channels to allow sand to accumulate for harvesting and commercial sale, thereby worsening flooding and damaging public infrastructure. The commissioner explained that some roads remained in good condition until the recent heavy rainy season, which he said exposed the effects of underground water that had not been adequately captured in the initial construction data. “Many of the roads were designed and built and they never became bad until this year’s heavy rainy season. It’s the underground water that is the cause of the road damage, as the data we used did not capture the volume of the underground water,” he said. He added that the effects of underground water were also visible in residential buildings, where ground-floor surfaces were reportedly peeling. On allegations of poor construction standards and the engagement of unqualified contractors, Ezeobi maintained that the government had carefully selected reputable construction firms to handle its projects. He described the contractors as A-rated companies, saying they had the capacity to return to sites and carry out reconstruction whenever defects occurred. According to him, the affected contractors were undertaking the repairs at no additional cost to the state government. He, however, acknowledged that human errors could not be completely ruled out as a possible cause of some road failures. The commissioner cited the Amawbia-Ekwulobi

item.title: Tambuwal accuses APC of failing Nigerians
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of failing Nigerians, citing worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country. Tambuwal made the allegations at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the opposition party as an alternative to the ruling APC. Addressing party supporters at the rally, the former governor said the APC had failed to provide the leadership needed to address the country’s economic and security challenges. He argued that millions of Nigerians were grappling with worsening economic difficulties, widespread hunger and persistent insecurity, which he said had exposed the ruling party’s inability to govern effectively. Tambuwal maintained that Nigerians deserved a government capable of guaranteeing security, economic stability and better living conditions. He urged citizens to embrace the ADC, describing the party as an alternative capable of addressing the country’s pressing challenges. The former governor’s remarks came amid intensifying political exchanges ahead of the 2027 general elections. He called on Nigerians to rally behind the ADC and its presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, to change the country’s political direction. item.title: NASA Space Grant Students Fuel Agency’s Inspiration Tour
item.description: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman addresses a standing-room-only crowd during an Inspiration Tour stop at Iowa State University. Credit: NASA NASA’s Inspiration Tour spread the excitement of space exploration and aeronautical innovation by connecting the public, industry, and academia with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space. At nearly every stop across the country, NASA Space Grant has brought students into the heart of the action. In Iowa, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman toured the Make to Innovate program lab at Iowa State University. Students from the Iowa Space Grant Consortium’s Mission Moon program, along with consortium-funded student organizations including Cardinal Space Mining, CySat, and CyLaunch, shared research findings and demonstrated the institution’s strong connection to NASA via agency-funded projects. During a well-attended town hall event NASA experts briefed students on the agency’s Moon Base efforts and how their work can contribute to future exploration. “We’re grateful for the opportunity to welcome NASA leadership to Iowa State,” said Sara Nelson Iowa Space Grant director. “The excitement among students was incredible, and the visit highlighted how the research and innovation happening in Iowa can help advance Artemis and NASA’s future exploration efforts.” At the University of Arizona, the NASA administrator saw firsthand the space research and engineering capabilities that are enabled by the Arizona Space Grant Consortium. From satellite communications testing to complex optics for peering into deep space to student-built high-altitude balloon payloads and even small satellites, students at the University of Arizona have a long history of contributing to NASA missions and making aerospace career connections. This tour stop also included a Q&A session where the NASA administrator answered questions from local high school and college students. “It was incredible to present the high-altitude ballooning research we do in SEDS (Students for the Exploration and Development of Space) to Jared Isaacman and those at NASA,” said Ella Miller, a junior studying mechanical engineering at the University of Arizona. “Arizona Space Grant has allowed me to get hands-on experience through an entire mission design process every semester, helping me pursue a career in space research and secure internships in this field.” Space Grant students from the University of Alaska Fairbanks shared their research with NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a Science Fair event in conjunction with the agency’s Inspiration Tour stop. Credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls At the University of Alaska in Fairbanks, the Administrator toured two Geophysical Institute facilities: Poker Flat Research Range, the university’s scientific rocket launching facility, and the Alaska Satellite Facility. item.title: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist
item.description: The hackers who stole billions of dollars in cryptocurrency from the Binance exchange spent months working on the theft and used both social engineering and novel malware in the process, the company said Tuesday. The heist, which both the FBI and the TRM Security firm attributed to North Korean actors, initially targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance wallets. The exchange has since frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of that sum. Binance said it has set aside funds required to cover the loss and provided this link to a Proof of Reserves page. The $6.34 billion represents the biggest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft. Advanced persistent threat Binance said the people behind the heist began no later than June and continued until last Thursday, when they successfully compromised an engineer's laptop and withdrew assets from several wallets. Like just about every organization that suffers a public, high-consequence hack, Binance said the threat actor was sophisticated and resourceful. Read full article Comments

item.title: TD Cowen: Democratic Sweep Makes a Crypto-Backed CLARITY Act ‘Impossible’
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen: Democratic Sweep Makes a Crypto-Backed CLARITY Act ‘Impossible’ The Democratic sweep of Congress closes the door on crypto market structure legislation like the Clarity Act for the next two years and may rule out any version the industry would support, TD Cowen told clients in a note published after the Associated Press called both chambers. “We view this outcome as negative for our sectors,” Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg wrote. The caveat he has repeated all cycle still holds: the election “will not impact the ability of regulators to push their de-regulatory agendas,” and he expects the SEC and CFTC “to remain active including on crypto, prediction markets and perps.” The items he flags to watch are the lame-duck session, congressional investigations of Trump, the debt ceiling and populist bills such as interest rate caps. The note lands after a bruising week for the industry: a record $6.34 billion Binance hack , the loss of House allies Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn and Ann Wagner, and more than $170 million in super PAC spending that failed to deliver the Congress it was meant to buy. Clarity, Brown and World Liberty Seiberg’s crypto calls build on a note he published Tuesday , before the results. Sherrod Brown’s return to the Senate from Ohio, after about $64 million in industry money went to stopping him, “damages the crypto industry’s political clout,” he wrote. He had not expected the CLARITY Act to pass in the next Congress; Brown’s win “makes us more confident in our prediction.” The bill, which passed the House in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 in September, dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it. Seiberg goes further than most: Democratic investigations of the Trump family’s crypto ventures, including World Liberty Financial, “may make it impossible to advance a version of Clarity that the crypto sector could back.” That shifts the question from timing to whether any bill the industry wants can pass under this Congress. The agencies are the counterweight. Seiberg sees no change at the SEC or CFTC, which have cleared bitcoin perpetuals , equity perps and a joint crypto taxonomy this year without Congress. The CME lawsuit over the perps approval is the live threat to that path, not the election. Debt ceiling, confirmations and the Fed The rest of the note reads as macro risk for an asset that has traded with the Nasdaq all autumn. Seiberg expects a push to raise the debt ceiling in the lame duck but doubts it succeeds, since Democrats will want the vote as leverage next year. Divided government raises the odds of a shutdown or default standoff in 2027. He sees Trump and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the likely Senate Banking chair, finding common ground on an interest rate cap, closer to 36% than the 10% Trump has floated, with fintechs more exposed than banks. Two items touch the Fed. Seiberg does not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees unless the president fills Democratic seat

item.title: What I learned driving the Slate electric truck prototype
item.description: If my 45-minute drive yesterday morning is anything to go by, I think Slate Auto will have quite the hit on its hands. The startup had one of its prototype trucks in town and asked if I wanted to check it out—no jumping on a plane or having to spend yet another night in an interchangeable hotel room, just a drive from southwest DC to Rockville, Maryland. Easy-peasy. The prototype truck had been well-used, with almost 6,000 miles (9,656 km) showing on the small and minimalist but very legible digital display that also shows your speed and, if you engage reverse, the backup camera. And while the cabin layout was representative of the production version, the surfaces most certainly weren’t—the prototype instead uses a lot of hard and shiny black plastic, with strips of Velcro here and there left over from when the interior had to be camouflaged when the vehicle was out in public. Getting acquainted with the Slate was refreshingly easy. The Morris Marina-like door handles open with a pleasing mechanical action. The seat and steering column adjust manually but with plenty of reach, something many budget models used to leave out to save on cost. Read full article Comments

item.title: US gov IT worker pleads guilty to sending Top Secret files to Ethiopia
item.description: He swore an allegiance to the US, but he was working for someone else. An IT specialist who worked across US government departments and held Top Secret clearance has pleaded guilty to transmitting sensitive documents to Ethiopia. Abraham Teklu Lemma, 53, admitted to the espionage offenses and agreed to a prison term between 120 and 262 months, the Justice Department confirmed on Tuesday. A naturalized citizen of the US, Lemma, of Maryland, had worked for the US government in different capacities and across different teams, including for the National Reconnaissance Office, State Department (DoS), and Justice Department (DoJ), between 2019 and 2023. These roles included working evening hours as an IT help desk technician at the DoS as of 2021, and daytime work at the DoJ as a contract management analyst, according to court documents. Lemma had what's known as "downdraft" authority, which is to say that he was permitted to move classified files between classified systems, and unclassified files from classified to unclassified systems. Crucially, he was only allowed to access classified files on non-DoS systems with written approval that it was part of his official duties, and worked in a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) – a secure workplace built for handling classified files. The criminal complaint [PDF] initially stated that the alleged offending began in July 2022, although the DoJ more recently claimed that it began in 2021. It claims Lemma was caught trawling "several" non-DoS classified portals and accessed intelligence reports without the proper authorization to do so. On various occasions, Lemma, who had held Top Secret security clearance since 2020, copied information from at least 133 intelligence reports without need-to-know authorization, according to court documents. Prosecutors claimed that the man downloaded more than 100 documents, burned them to CD/DVDs, and deleted their classification markings. The material Lemma was copying was at the Secret and Top Secret levels, but burned onto discs with green labels, which are approved for employees and are supposed to signify the contents of the discs relating to unclassified material only. Lemma would allegedly take these discs at the end of his shift and exit the SCIF with them tucked into his jacket pocket. On other occasions, he was observed looking at classified material on his PC, then taking handwritten notes before folding the paper and again storing it in his pocket. This continued until around August 2023. Prosecutors claimed that Lemma began transmitting information to Ethiopian officials via an encrypted messaging app in or around August and September 2022, weeks after the alleged offending began. The files included documents, photographs, notes, maps, and information relating to Ethiopia, and officials would ask Lemma to provide details about command centers, logistics centers, military compounds, and other matters. item.title: Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, for Abuja after completing his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the holy city of Makkah. According to a statement by the presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President’s aircraft took off from the Royal Terminal of the airport at exactly 5:13 p.m. Saudi time. Onanuga said the Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Consul-General, Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the President to the airport. Before his departure, Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. ﻿ The President had earlier led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers. Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the President offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom and strength to continue serving the Nigerian people. He also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would become a source of strength, national cohesion and shared prosperity. Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport before departing Saudi Arabia. Onanuga said the President’s visit to Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving and prayers for Nigeria, as well as a renewed commitment to building a peaceful, united and prosperous nation. The statement added that Tinubu expressed profound appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and the Nigerian delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers. “President Tinubu left the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with renewed faith, gratitude to Almighty Allah and an unwavering commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda and the aspiration of building a better Nigeria for all,” the statement said. Those in the President’s entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. The post Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Riot (RIOT) and Hut 8 (HUT) Sell Thousands of Bitcoin to Fund AI Ventures, Share Buybacks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Riot (RIOT) and Hut 8 (HUT) Sell Thousands of Bitcoin to Fund AI Ventures, Share Buybacks Two of the largest public bitcoin miners reported third-quarter results on Wednesday, and both used the occasion to confirm they have been selling the asset they were built to accumulate. Riot Platforms has sold 20,264 BTC this year for about $1.5 billion, and Hut 8 has sold 3,102 BTC since July to fund $250 million in share repurchases. The sales serve different ends. Riot is paying for data center construction; Hut 8 is buying back its own stock. Riot ended September with 2,418 BTC, worth about $202 million at the quarter-end price of $83,554. It held 18,005 at the start of the year. Hut 8 reported about 16,787 BTC across the parent and its majority-owned American Bitcoin on Sept. 30, worth $1.4 billion, of which $697.4 million was attributable to Hut 8 itself, before October sales reduced the parent’s share. Riot: the treasury becomes a construction budget Riot’s selling has been steady all year. It sold 3,778 bitcoin in the first quarter, about 2.5 times its production, then 4,300 in the second and a further 12,186 in the third. The proceeds funded data center work and the full repayment of a $200 million Coinbase credit facility, which released all pledged coins. The company raised no equity in 2026. The reason arrived with the results. Riot signed a 15-year triple-net lease with an unnamed “Frontier AI Lab” for the whole of its Corsicana, Texas campus, 910 MW of critical IT capacity, worth about $28 billion over the initial term and $1.8 billion in average annual rent. Combined with its AMD contract and an earlier Rockdale lease with the same tenant, Riot has leased 1,151 MW for about $38 billion. CEO Jason Les put expected net operating income above $2 billion a year at full deployment, according to the company release. The structure limits Riot’s outlay. Capital cost is about $6 million per MW, half a typical Tier 3 build; Riot funds $2 million of that for site work and power, and the tenant covers the rest, to be reimbursed from non-recourse project debt after each phase is delivered. Delivery runs from September 2027 to July 2028. Mining continues in the background. Riot produced 1,637 BTC in the quarter at an average cost of $39,265 before depreciation, but mining revenue fell 28% to $116 million as the average price dropped to $70,855 from $114,361 a year earlier. Total revenue was $181.4 million, flat year over year, with data center and engineering income filling the gap. Hut 8: bitcoin out, shares in Hut 8’s sales went to shareholders rather than contractors. It sold about 954 bitcoin for $74.8 million in the quarter and about 2,148 BTC for $175.4 million in October, retiring 3.3 million shares for a combined $250 million. On Nov. 2 the board raised the repurchase authorization to $1 billion. item.title: The DEA banned a drug some opioid users called a miracle
item.description: In 2012, as the driver of deaths in the opioid crisis began moving from prescription pills to heroin, Laura Bohn was tasked with finding safer drugs to manage pain. Funded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse, in 2017 she and other scientists revealed in the science journal Cell that several compounds—including a particularly promising one called SR-17018—could relieve pain in mice without causing respiratory depression. That’s a big deal, because respiratory depression is typically what causes people using opioids to stop breathing and die. Bohn, senior associate vice president of research at University of South Florida Health, says her team filed a patent on SR-17018. They went on to discover that mice using the chemical did not develop a high tolerance for it and that mice already dependent on morphine—a powerful opioid—could consume SR-17018 to reset their tolerance without suffering from painful withdrawal symptoms. item.title: Why the weirdest game of 2026 is also one of my favourites
item.description: Titanium Court is a bizarre world of 8-bit fairies, Shakespeare and surprise songs – its magic lies in never knowing what on earth is going on • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court . It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths. At the end of this late-night run, I met a boss I’d defeated before – a comically hungry dragon – and the game asked if I would like to skip the boss fight and enjoy a musical performance instead. A game has never asked me this before. Of course, I accepted. And then, instead of the familiar tiled battlefield, I was looking at a pixellated singer-songwriter, who launched into an extremely long preamble about the mating habits of the Pacific salmon before saying, “This is a song for anyone else who ever got so horny they could die,” and launching into a soulful acoustic guitar number accompanied by crude images of leaping fish. I began to wonder if my meds were making me hallucinate. Continue reading...

item.title: Students gather to explore Hawaii's glorious night sky | Space photo of the day for Nov. 4, 2026
item.description: null Over 1,400 students gathered in Hawaii to learn about astronomy as part of the annual Journey Through the Universe program. (Image credit: NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/J. Pollard) Students gathered under the stars in Hawaii recently to explore the awesome nature of the night sky together. What is it? From Oct. 19 to Oct. 22, more than 1,400 students on the Big Island of Hawaii gathered for the Journey Through the Universe event to explore astronomy together. The Journey Through the Universe program is currently in its 23rd year. It was originally developed by the National Center for Earth and Space Science Education (NCESSE) and later introduced in Hawaii by the international Gemini Observatory, a program within the U.S. National Science Foundation's NOIRLab (National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory) that works with the Department of Education Hilo-Waiākea. The program aims to introduce students in the Hilo-Waiākea public school system to astronomy as well as the incredible science that happens across Hawaii. The students who participate range from preschoolers to seniors in high school, so the program introduces some students to astronomy and helps others explore possible careers in STEM fields. This year, the program brought in 19 volunteer educators from scientific institutions like Maunakea Observatories and supported hands-on activities and lessons that went from the classroom to under the Milky Way . Why is it incredible? This image shows a growing love for astronomy in progress. From the red glow of a skywatching night (red light doesn't interfere with our ability to see at night like white light does) to the scattered telescopes and students standing under the stars, this scene paints a larger picture. This is just one program, but in bringing together volunteers, educators, scientists and students, the program has created an incredible and enduring learning experience. Whether or not students walk away wanting to pursue a career in STEM, this incredible immersion in astronomy can help to foster a lifelong appreciation for science and nature. It's always a great idea to gather under the stars and explore together.

item.title: HP Inc hires former GSK boss as CEO
item.description: HP Inc has hired former GSK boss Emma Walmsley to plot its course through choppy PC and print waters. Walmsley spent eight years as the boss at pharma biz GSK and further back in time held various marketing and general management positions at L'Oreal. She has no track record running a tech company, though she was on Microsoft’s board. “Throughout the process, Emma stood out for the strength of her leadership experience across multiple industries, the clarity of her strategic thinking and her ability to translate customer insights into new growth,” said Chip Bergh, chair of HP's board. In the first nine months of HP's fiscal 2026 , revenue had jumped 10 percent year-on-year to $44.5 billion. The print business shrank in that time and PCs generated the growth. However, amid a memory crunch with supplies dwindling, analysts are forecasting PC market contraction in terms of unit sales. Global PC shipments slumped 20 percent in Q3 as DRAM shortages forced up prices and customers opted instead to sweat their assets rather than replace their fleet of computers. Things aren't expected to improve in the final three months of 2026. One beacon of hope for all PC makers was AI, yet many customers aren't buying into the story for various reasons. Walmsley previously said that during her time at the top of GSK she created a "totally different company, in platform, in momentum, in talent, in culture," she told the FT . "I think in time… it will be recognized." She also dealt with activist investor Elliot Management, which operates in the tech industry and called for her to reapply for the CEO role at GSK, claiming her lack of science background was an issue. Walmsley said: " HP is an iconic company with a defining role in shaping the future of work on a global scale. I’m excited to join the team and, together, move forward with clarity and conviction. We will focus on harnessing the power of the AI era and putting HP’s creativity and innovation to work to unlock new sources of growth and deliver lasting value for our customers, shareholders, partners and people." Employees will be crossing their fingers that their new boss doesn’t borrow from the playbook of her predecessor - who hotfooted it to PayPal in February - by running multiple redundancy rounds, and shareholders will hope their stock price show sustainable improvement. If not, Walmsley may have to manage more interest from activist investors at the latest corporation she is running. ®

item.title: Circle (CRCL) Cuts About 5% of Workforce as Q3 Revenue Hits $865M
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Circle (CRCL) Cuts About 5% of Workforce as Q3 Revenue Hits $865M Circle Internet Group cut about 5% of its workforce in the third quarter, a reduction the USDC issuer disclosed in the footnotes of an earnings report that showed revenue rising 17% to $865 million and net income up 5% to $226 million. The company booked a $9.1 million restructuring charge for the cuts, which it described as “designed to better align our organizational structure with our operating model and strategic priorities.” The charge covered notice-period pay, severance and benefits. Circle did not say how many employees were affected or which teams were hit, and the layoffs did not appear in the release’s list of business highlights. CRCL shares slipped about 1.2% in premarket trading to $74.33 after gaining 4.4% on Tuesday. The stock trades at a fraction of the highs it reached after its June 2025 IPO. A token sale carried the quarter The headline growth masks a softer core. Reserve income, the interest Circle earns on the Treasuries and cash backing USDC, fell 8% from a year earlier to $658 million as the reserve return rate dropped 61 basis points to 3.5%. Average USDC in circulation grew 8% to $73.3 billion, not enough to offset lower yields, and circulation at quarter-end was flat year over year at $73.9 billion. Circle’s share of the fiat-backed stablecoin market slipped to 27%. What filled the gap was a one-time item. Other revenue jumped to $207 million from $29 million, with $182 million of that from the private presale of ARC, the token for Circle’s new Arc blockchain. Strip that out and total revenue would have declined. Adjusted EBITDA of $317 million, up 85%, carries the same presale. The cost side tells the rest. Operating expenses rose 16% to $245 million on higher general and administrative, depreciation, IT and marketing spending, while distribution costs, the fees Circle pays partners such as Coinbase to hold USDC, fell 8% to $409 million. The workforce cut lands as the company builds Arc, integrates a January asset acquisition and prepares to absorb Tazapay. Circle is spending on the next business Circle is paying for growth outside its core product. Arc’s public mainnet launched Sept. 16 with more than 100 institutional builders, and Circle minted the full 10 billion ARC supply, becoming the first public company to issue a network token for its own layer-one chain. It agreed to buy Tazapay, a Singapore cross-border payments platform with more than $25 billion in annualized volume, in a deal expected to close in 2027. Binance, days before its $6.34 billion hack , put $100 million into Circle equity and renewed a USDC distribution partnership. The GENIUS Act takes effect Jan. 18, bringing federal licensing and reserve rules for stablecoin issuers, a regime the Federal Reserve has begun to fill in. Circle has said its stablecoins will qualify. Whether a smaller headcount and a one-time token windfall can bridge the gap until rates stop fall

item.title: Lagos Opens Legal Research Centre, Targets Stronger Justice Delivery
item.description: The Lagos State Government has opened a Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training, describing it as a strategic investment to strengthen the justice system, develop legal expertise and prepare the state’s justice institutions for emerging challenges. Established by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice, the Centre is expected to serve as a hub for legal research, professional training, policy development and capacity building for practitioners and public officials in the justice sector. Speaking at the official opening ceremony in Alausa, Ikeja, on Wednesday, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN, described the facility as more than another government building, saying it represents a deliberate investment in knowledge, institutional excellence and the future of justice administration in Lagos State. “There are occasions when we open a building or office. There are other occasions when we open a door to the future. Today, in Lagos, we are doing the latter — opening a door to the future,” Pedro said. He described the Centre as the first of its kind within a Ministry of Justice in Nigeria, arguing that a justice system that intends to remain relevant and effective must continually educate, examine and reform itself. Dignitaries at the opening of the Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training in Lagos. Pedro said the initiative aligns with the broader development agenda of the Sanwo-Olu administration, noting that the development of Lagos cannot be separated from strong institutions and an efficient administration of justice. He identified the rule of law, access to justice and capable institutions as essential foundations for economic development, good governance and social inclusion. The Attorney-General also linked the Centre to the administration’s THEMES Plus Agenda, stressing that building a secure, economically vibrant and inclusive society requires sustained investment in the people and institutions responsible for interpreting, administering and developing the state’s laws. He said the Centre would help address the growing demands of a modern justice system, including the need for continuous professional development, evidence-based policy and institutional reform. Outlining its proposed operational framework, Pedro disclosed that the Ministry intends to incorporate the Centre as a not-for-profit entity under a public-private partnership arrangement. Under the proposed structure, the Ministry of Justice and its private-sector partners will jointly manage the Centre’s day-to-day operations. While the government will provide policy direction, legitimacy and strategic oversight, the private sector is expected to contribute funding, technical expertise, innovation and operational efficiency. Pedro said the arrangement was designed to ensure the Centre’s sustainability and effectiveness. The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN. item.title: Bitcoin Price Soars Above $79,000 After Democratic Sweep of Congress
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Soars Above $79,000 After Democratic Sweep of Congress Bitcoin price traded near $79,200 on Wednesday morning, up about 2% on the day, after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections and dealt the crypto industry its worst night in Washington since 2022. The Associated Press called the Senate for Democrats late Tuesday and the House early Wednesday. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become speaker. The result exceeded most forecasts: by Wednesday morning the AP tracker showed Democrats with 54 Senate seats to Republicans’ 44, with races still open. Prediction markets had put a Democratic House above 90% for weeks, but the Senate margin and the loss of several Republican crypto allies in the House came as a surprise. The bitcoin price reacted in two moves. Bitcoin fell to $75,618, a seven-week low, as results came in during Asian trading, then recovered the full loss and more by the European open. Traders broadly speaking treated the sweep as the removal of a known risk rather than a shock: prediction markets had priced a Democratic win for weeks, and options desks saw heavy call buying on election day, with block volume more than double the prior session. The view on the desks is that a Democratic Congress is less friendly to crypto legislation but that divided government, a presidential veto and executive orders cap how much policy can change, leaving technical targets near $82,000 as the next test. Demand remains the weak point, with U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shedding about $1.16 billion over three sessions and the price still about 27% below where it stood a year ago, down from about $80,500 a week before the vote. The races that cost bitcoin and crypto The industry’s super PACs spent more than $170 million this cycle, most of it for Republicans, and the headline bets failed. Sherrod Brown won back an Ohio Senate seat in a special election against Sen. Jon Husted despite about $64 million in crypto money aimed at stopping him, the largest sum the industry has spent against any single candidate. Brown chaired the Senate Banking Committee until his 2024 defeat and spent that tenure resisting market structure bills. Senate seniority rules may limit his path back to a gavel, but he returns to a chamber his party controls. Three House Republicans the industry counted on lost their seats: Bryan Steil of Wisconsin, who fell to ER nurse Mitchell Berman; Zach Nunn of Iowa; and Ann Wagner of Missouri. Stand With Crypto had endorsed Steil and Nunn and directed ad money to both. Mike Lawler of New York conceded to Democrat Cait Conley with the race uncalled. House Financial Services Chairman French Hill appears to have held his Arkansas seat but will hand the gavel to Rep. Maxine Waters. item.title: US Midterm Voters Deliver Brutal Verdict On Trump
item.description: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran. The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments. The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. “This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back,” Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results. “I think the Democrats did a good job,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.” Combo image of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (r) and President of the U.S Donald Trump (l) But he sought to distance himself from his party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration. Republican Heartland Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008. In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor’s race, ending decades of Republican rule. Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers. In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024. item.title: US midterm candidates find something to agree on: Reining in datacenters
item.description: Datacenter restrictions found broad support among candidates for governor in this week's US midterm elections, with nearly all those examined by Data Center Watch backing bans, pauses, or tighter development rules. Data Center Watch, which tracks grassroots opposition to compute sheds across America, examined the public positions of 74 selected candidates across the 36 states that elected governors in the midterm elections on November 3. It found that 43 percent of those candidates supported a ban or moratorium on new projects, while another 51 percent backed further regulation or conditional development. Only about 5 percent had no stated public position. Support for bans or moratoriums crossed party lines, although it was more common among the Democratic candidates examined (60 percent) than Republicans (30 percent). Candidates from both major parties backed restrictions in eight states: Maryland, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, Ohio, Oregon, Wisconsin, and Texas. Texas has experienced a boom in data campus development recently, thanks to its ample energy resources and light-touch regulations, although outgoing governor Greg Abbott ordered a pause earlier this year while audits of energy and water use were carried out. Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Abbott in Tuesday's election and will take office in January. Those positions matter to developers because governors can shape state regulation, energy policy, and permitting, although approval powers vary by jurisdiction. However, temporary pauses and targeted construction restrictions do not necessarily amount to opposition to all datacenter development. Things were even starker where folk got to vote directly on the issue, with measures regarding datacenters appearing on the ballot as well as candidates. Data Centers on the Ballot , which tracked many of these, found that 43 out of 46 municipalities where tighter restrictions on server farms were up for a vote had approved those at the time of publication. Only in one case, the City of Harwood in North Dakota, had restrictions been rejected, and 2 had yet to post results. AI-related campaign spending has also come under scrutiny. Guardrails Alliance, a labor-backed pressure group, described Leading the Future , a super PAC network opposing AI regulation, as "largely a non-factor" in the elections . It alleged the network avoided the most competitive races because "they know their money is politically toxic." Anti-datacenter sentiment has grown in the US in response to the facilities popping up in people's backyards, often without them having any say in the process. A Gallup survey earlier this year discovered that more than 70 percent of Americans would be against the construction of one in their neighborhood, while a Pew Research Center survey found that Americans increasingly believe datacenters are bad for the environment and blame them for rising household energy bills. item.title: How military reduced nationwide attacks by 73 per cent in October as 217 terrorists neutralised
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian military have drastically reduced attacks across various theatres of operations in October 2026, Daily Trust reports. Checks showed that only 98 attacks were recorded during the month under review, representing a 73.3 per cent decline from the 367 attacks recorded in September. A breakdown of the October figures showed that Operation Enduring Peace recorded the highest number of attacks with 29 incidents, followed by Operation Hadin Kai with 27 and Operation Fansan Yamma with 24. Operation Whirl Stroke recorded 12 attacks, while Operation Udo Ka recorded four. Operations Delta Safe and Savannah Shield recorded one attack each. Specifically, the October figure represents a decline of 269 attacks compared with the previous month’s total of 367. This is just as the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, assured Nigerians that the military would intensify efforts to apprehend those responsible for the attacks and bring them to justice. Oluyede also urged troops to remain disciplined, uphold the rules of engagement and respect human rights, while warning against complacency, particularly as the festive season approaches. He called on security agencies to strengthen intelligence sharing and joint planning, while urging community leaders and residents to report suspicious activities to security formations or through the military’s toll-free line, 193. Providing updates for Nigerians on military operations across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja, revealed that many kidnapped victims would continue to be freed from captivity. “During the period under review, the AFN recorded a total of 98 attacks across various theatres of operation. Operation HADIN KAI recorded 27 attacks, Operation FANSAN YAMMA recorded 24, Operation ENDURING PEACE recorded 29, Operation WHIRL STROKE recorded 12, Operation UDO KA (OPUK) recorded 4, while Operation DELTA SAFE and Operation SAVANNAH SHIELD recorded 1 attack each,” the breakdown was contained in a document released on Friday. Earlier in September, Operation Enduring Peace recorded 147 attacks, Operation Fansan Yamma 115, Operation Whirl Stroke 55, Operation Hadin Kai 33, Operation Savannah Shield 13 and Operation Udo Ka four, while Operation Delta Safe recorded none. The senior military officer explained that troops neutralised more than 217 terrorists and criminals, arrested 333 suspects and rescued 349 kidnap victims during the month. He added that 70 insurgents surrendered to troops, while 105 arms and 3,174 rounds of ammunition were recovered. Onoja said the military also recovered 756,837 litres of stolen crude oil products and destroyed 49 illegal refining sites during operations against crude oil theft. “Throughout the month, over 217 terrorists and criminals were neutralized, with 333 terrorist/criminals arrested and 349 kidnap victims rescued. “Additionally, 70 insurgents surrendered to troops, while 105 arms and 3174 rounds of ammuni

Just as the Watergate scandal helped propel a new generation of Democratic lawmakers into Congress in 1974, Zian argues that public disillusionment with the Iran war, mounting economic pressures and dissatisfaction with Donald Trump's leadership may now be reshaping the American political landscape. item.title: Drone warfare in space: Swarms of autonomous, laser-shooting cubesats could defend Western satellites in orbit
item.description:
Mark is an award-winning freelance aviation and space journalist and author of the non-fiction book "N-4 DOWN: The Hunt for the Arctic airship Italia." He began writing for Space.com in 2026 and writes for a range of publications, from BBC Future to The Smithsonian’s Air and Space Quarterly and others. Mark won awards two years in a row at the Aerospace Media Awards for features he had written on the history of drones and astronaut training. Space grabbed hold of Mark’s imagination when, as a child, he saw the opening scene of "Star Wars: A New Hope" for the first time and has never let go. Away from the final frontier, Mark can be found walking his dog along the country lanes of England’s Cotswolds.

In May 2026, four Russian military satellites came close to ICEYE-X36, a private synthetic aperture radar satellite widely believed to be providing battlefield intelligence for Ukraine, in an apparently aggressive and risky "grey zone" maneuver that spooked many in the space industry. Close enough to jam or interfere with the satellite's signal, blind it with a laser, fire a metal dart at it or, simply, force it to maneuver and burn fuel, the satellites' seemingly intimidatory behavior has increased the West's desire to develop defensive technology for satellites . In October 2026, it was reported that one of those same four Russian satellites passed within 500 meters (1,650 feet) of the same ICEYE satellite. Now, U.K. startup Shield Space is racing to apply the lessons of drone warfare in Ukraine to develop swarms of up to 100 very small, low-cost, attritable drone-like autonomous spacecraft called cubesats . Released by a car-sized carrier in Earth orbit, these microwave-sized spacecraft will act as interceptors to protect Western satellites , and their deployment will mark a next step in the evolution of orbital warfare . Shield Space says that these space drones will use "effectors" like lasers or microwaves, or "kinetic standoff" techniques, to defend Western satellites even if controllers lose contact with them. "We're talking about deploying 100 cubesats on a protect-and-defend mission for less than £100 million [$134 million US], which is how [much] you would pay for one satellite previously," said Graeme Ritchie, co-founder and CEO of Shield Space. Launched in 2023, NASA's civilian project Starling demonstrated that a swarm of four small satellites can cooperate and operate autonomously in space on a civilian science mission without relying heavily on real-time commands from ground control. But that seems like a far cry from the adversarial or defensive missions Shield Space and its competitors imagine. It is telling that the leading space powers appear not to have demonstrated swarm combat in space — although they tend to be reluctant to reveal their space warfare capabilities. Watchdog sticks probe into Capita's handling of 1.7 million member civil service pension scheme
item.description: Capita has repeatedly "broken" promises to resolve the "chaos" engulfing the Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) following its takeover of the administration – a move that left thousands of retired public sector workers unpaid. So says Parliamentary spending watchdog, the Public Accounts Committee, which this week launched an inquiry into the handover of the ten-year £239 million contract in December from previous incumbent MyCSP. As The Register exclusively revealed , the troubles began early on as members of CSPS – which manages pensions for 1.7 million people – complained of unrecognized passwords and usernames on the portal Capita developed. Capita said it inherited 132,100 complex remediation cases, and claimed the work-in-progress backlog from the prior system was more than double the 37,000 items when it won the deal in 2023 . Capita ran to Microsoft for support , and promised the use AI and automation, in addition to its 500 full-time employees working on the project, would resolve the issues by March. It missed this deadline, as well as one set for June 30 and is set to miss March 2027 . The government subsequently withheld a £10 million payment to Capita over the CSPS fiasco. The National Audit Office, a spending regulator, has already launched its own probe into the failures and is now joined by the PAC, which says thousands of civil servants and their families have struggled to on and collect their pensions The PAC has already held three evidence sessions on Capita and the government’s efforts to ameliorate the situation. The law was changed in the Budget 2026 to mitigate the impact of administrative delays in CSPS on bereaved families. Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair at the PAC, said in a statement: "In response to the alarming reports of hard-working civil servants being thrown into financial uncertainty following Capita’s takeover of the CSPS, we have held a number of evidence sessions with both the top leadership of Capita, and the civil servants and ministers of the Cabinet Office who have ultimate responsibility for overseeing the contract. " Over and over again, promises have been made and broken by Capita, to our faces in formal evidence sessions, that they will get a grip on what has gone wrong. As a result, we are launching an inquiry, which will be informed by the authoritative factual basis provided by the NAO, which supports the scrutiny work of this Committee." The inquiry will draw on the finding of the NAO's forthcoming report on the switch of CSPS to Capita, and will take into consideration the status of the scheme at go-live date, how Capita has performed, and the effect on CSPS members, plus take a look into the way the Cabinet Office has overseen the prior scheme and the switch to Capita. ® Updated to add at 1407 UTC: Capita has been in touch to say how "deeply sorry" it is about the "frustration" that the administration of the Civil Service Pension Scheme "has caused members and their families." item.title: Cyberattack on French plasma stores is enough to make your blood boil
item.description: Attackers tampered with cold-storage settings used by France's civilian blood service after compromising a refrigeration supplier, the organization said. The French Blood Establishment (EFS) confirmed the incident on Tuesday, saying its own systems had not been directly targeted. Safeguards prevented any loss of blood products. The affected equipment stored blood samples and frozen plasma, including plasma intended for transfusion. "The EFS' monitoring and alarm systems enabled the rapid identification of these anomalies and the implementation of necessary measures to ensure that no blood samples or products were compromised," it said. "Thus, depending on the circumstances, as soon as the incident occurred, the affected equipment was either brought under control without impacting the products and samples, or neutralized; the products stored in these cold rooms were preventively transferred to other facilities." The EFS did not name the supplier publicly. According to reports, attackers changed cold-room temperature settings from -30°C to 110°C. That does not mean the equipment or its contents reached the higher temperature. The organization added that it notified the country's cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, and the Ministry of Health. News about cyberattacks targeting refrigeration devices across Europe emerged on Monday morning after retailers arrived to work, only to find puddles on the floor after cyber criminals activated defrost modes. Reports of the supermarket attacks describe remotely activated defrost cycles and temperatures as high as 50°C, forcing retailers to discard spoiled food. The attackers have not been identified. More retailers have reported disruption since the initial disclosures on Monday. Stores across Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden were the first to report issues, although cases from Estonia, Finland, Germany, Portugal, Romania, and the Netherlands have since been confirmed. Richard Horne, chief executive of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), told BBC Radio 4's Today program on Wednesday that he was aware of "a couple of impacts" in the UK's own food supply chain. No affected UK businesses have publicly identified themselves, although the British Association of Independent Meat Suppliers (AIMS) told the BBC that some of its more than 300 members had become "collateral" in the attacks, with two reporting that their fridges had begun defrosting. The latest wave of cold-store attacks comes a month after the first, which affected French supermarket chains Carrefour, Coopérative U, Intermarché, Monoprix, and others. Both supermarket waves involved remote interference with refrigeration controls, causing stock losses. Whether the attack affecting EFS used the same access route remains unclear. Some affected chains identified Danfoss controllers in their systems; others said they did not use the company's equipment. item.description: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo This ambitious remake transforms a landmark Zelda game into a modern masterpiece, clearer and easier to navigate, more beautiful to look at, with playful musical touches. Yet the melancholy remains It’s always a worry, returning to a formative piece of art from your childhood. Will your jaded adult sensibilities render you unable to locate the magic that captivated your child self? Will revisiting it reveal that it was never actually that good, and that your tastes are built on a foundation of lies? With video games, there is the added complication of technological advancement: decades-old games can look so basic and feel so treacly to play that it’s hard to explain why they were mind-blowing at the time. Light-touch remasters aim to bring such games up to modern graphical standards without fundamentally changing them; an ambitious remake attempts to transform the work into something that can stand alongside any modern masterpiece. Ocarina of Time is the latter. And I could not be more delighted to report that it is a dream come true. Continue reading...

item.title: The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show
item.description: null Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look. What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)? Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years. These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower : The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10. As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky. Both branches of the Taurid meteor shower appear to travel away from a point of origin — or radiant — located in the constellation Taurus , which rises in the southeastern sky during November evenings. The Taurids are known for spawning brilliant fireball meteors, which can flare brighter than Venus as pebble-sized pieces of debris enter and burn up in the atmosphere. When to look for Taurid shooting stars The Southern Taurid shower features two distinct yearly peaks, the first of which occurred on Oct. 14. The second takes place overnight on Nov. 4-5 and is associated with an increase in fireball activity, when up to five meteors per hour could be seen blazing across the sky. The Northern Taurid stream, meanwhile, is expected to peak overnight on Nov. 11-12 with the same predicted hourly rate of up to five meteors per hour streaking across the dark, near moonless sky. How to spot Taurid meteors Head out to a dark sky location around midnight on the night of the peaks, when the shower's radiant in the constellation Taurus is positioned high in the southeastern sky, maximizing the number of meteors that can be seen. Remember not to stare directly at the radiant. Meteors seen close to the constellation Taurus strike our planet almost head-on, and so will have the shortest trails. Instead, pick out a patch of sky a little distance away, where the shooting stars will be at their most eye-catching as they skim through Earth's atmosphere. These essential stargazing accessories can help make a meteor-hunting trip! (Image credit: Created in Canva by Daisy Dobrijevic) Never use a telescope or binoculars to hunt for meteors, you want to take in as much of the sky as possible, not limit your field of view! And be sure to wrap up warm and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to the dark — a vital and often overlooked step for anyone hoping to catch even the faintest of meteors. Check out our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography , along with our guide to capturing fast-moving meteors if you want to create a permanent memory of the next big shower. item.title: Achieving nirvana: Enlightenment 0.28 hits the desktop
item.description: Fresh on the desktop this week is a new version of Enlightenment as well the continuation of noughties hero KDE 3, the Trinity Desktop Environment, for those who prefer things a little old school. Enlightenment version 0.28 is the latest release of one of the older Linux graphical environments, which first appeared in 1997. Version 0.28 arrives nearly two years after the previous release – we reported on Enlightement 0.27 in January 2025. If you're not familiar with this venerable window manager, often referred to as just E, we refer you back to that article, which also explains Enlightenment's slightly strange version numbering scheme. Last time around we noted that its single-line release notes really didn't give us much to write about. The development team has made up for it this time, with some 68 lines of changes. It's both the same old E, and simultaneously a modern tool: it is still an X11 window manager, but it can also act as a Wayland compositor if you prefer. It offers conventional stacking resizable windows, but also can act as a tiling window manager if you prefer. On recent distros, it can now talk to the Pipewire audio server, and it can also work with NetworkManager to control network connections. This version delivers preliminary support for NetBSD too. This isn't really a tool for newbies or those looking for a simple easy desktop. A sign of its age is that the first-run wizard asks if you want windows to activate as soon as you move the mouse pointer over them. This was traditional 20th century Unix behavior, and in the early days of Linux it was called "focus-follows-mouse," but it's rarely seen today. E isn't a full desktop environment: it only offers a few of its own optional tools, such as the Ecrire text editor, Ephoto picture viewer, Evisum task manager, and Rage video player. Even its taskbar is optional. It is more like a basis for experienced users to customize and build their own environment around. Trinity is back The Trinity Desktop Environment has a rather lower learning curve: TDE is a port of the final version of KDE 3 to modern Linux. Proving old school is still cool, the project – which keeps the look and feel of 2005-era KDE 3.5 alive – has just announced TDE release 14.1.7 , with dozens of bug fixes and plenty of new features. Among these is a tweak to the kicker/taskbar: you can now scroll the taskbar using the mouse wheel, flicking through your open applications.This release drops support for Ubuntu 24.10 "Oracular Oriole" but adds support for the latest 26.10 "Stonking Stingray." Forks of older versions by users disenchanted with new versions are a recurring feature of the FOSS world, but they often tend to peter out after a while. TDE is one of the exceptions: we first reported on a new release in 2021 and again in 2023 . ®

item.title: Windows pushed AI PCs, but now it's hit a wall of RAM prices
item.description: Microsoft wants enterprise customers to start thinking about PC refreshes using the same mindset – and line in the budget – as AI investments. The problem? Rising component costs caused by the proliferation of AI datacenters mean many clients are delaying client refreshes. In a call to arms, Microsoft became the headline sponsor of the Canalys Forum in Barcelona early last month for the first time ever. Redmond needs distributors and resellers that convene at the event annually to get behind Copilot, Cowork and, more generally, AI computers. Mark Linton, corporate veep for Windows and Device Sales, took to the stage to preach to a room he is hoping to convert. "What we're seeing is the tokenomics of [AI] is getting very challenging," he said. "Having agents working on frontier models quickly becomes very expensive." Redmond's proposed solution is to use those massive LLMs where most needed, "the right model for the right job," running smaller models locally at the edge on Windows PCs. " My goal, if we're successful in pivoting Windows to the agentic platform, is to have PC spend be part of the AI spend versus just PC refresh budget," he said. "In an AI hybrid world, you'll be able to use edge devices, powerful PCs with lots of memory, lots of capability to run your AI workloads that are appropriate right there on the device. You keep the data locally. Of course, you don't have the token cost of the cloud. You have better latency, and you have more control." Copilot is merely a component. This is not only about customers using Microsoft "first-party software" – it's for all models and all agents to use Windows as the platform, added Linton. Goodness knows, Windows does need a shot in the arm. Microsoft last week reported profit and loss accounts for Q1 of its fiscal 2027 , ended September 30, and revenue in the Windows OEM and Devices division shrank 22 percent from last year to $3.55 billion. Microsoft warned revenue generated in its Q2 may be down 30 percent. " Growth will continue to be impacted by elevated inventory levels, PC market demand and a prior year comparable that benefited from Windows 10 end of support," Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on an earnings call. Market watcher IDC said calendar Q3 PC shipments sank to 62.7 million units , down 20.1 percent year-on-year, translating into 15.8 million fewer sales into distributors' warehouses. Tough macroeconomic conditions coupled with rising memory costs mean tough times for the PC industry. Omdia – which owns Canalys – said: " The impact of upstream component cost increases has now fully worked its way through to end-market pricing, with consumers and IT decision-makers responding accordingly." Reg readers know why component costs are going up. The datacenter construction frenzy meant memory chip makers could make more money from higher-margin HBM than conventional DRAM, prompting them to prioritize production of the former . item.title: Datacenter operators must win hearts and minds, not just permits
item.description: Schneider Electric sees no slowdown in its datacenter business, but says operators must be more open with communities about the power, water, and land their projects will consume. As a supplier of electrical infrastructure, cooling, and power distribution equipment, Schneider has a direct view of operators' spending plans – and a commercial interest in continued construction. Steven Carlini, vice president of innovation and datacenter, said Schneider's pipeline showed no slowdown. "And Schneider has a lot of agreements, supply chain agreements with the larger datacenter operators." Reports earlier this year suggested only half the capacity planned for 2026 is actually under construction in the US, and land being cleared for new bit barn projects has plateaued. Carlini nevertheless said US companies were building as fast as they could, contrasting that with planning bureaucracy and other obstacles in Europe. "But the one thing that I think is going to be the biggest change is the level of transparency from the operators when they're trying to secure permits and when they're requesting power," Carlini said. "The way the model traditionally worked in the US is the operators would negotiate with the local jurisdictions that were responsible for issuing the permits, and there would be non-disclosures involved, almost universally. So the residents where these datacenters were going to be built had no visibility into these projects until construction started." Opposition to datacenter construction has grown in the US. Campaign groups called for a moratorium on new facilities late last year, and New York state imposed a halt this summer. The sheer scale of the new builds has also alarmed many folk, with Meta's Hyperion facility, for example, planned to reach 5 GW of power capacity and cover an area equal to a significant chunk of Manhattan . A recent survey by think tank Pew Research Center found that Americans are increasingly wary of datacenters , with more than half saying they are bad for the environment, bad for household energy bills, and consume water resources for cooling. In response, companies building and operating compute sheds need to be more upfront about what effect their plans will have on the local area, Carlini said. "They're going to have to disclose where the power is going to come from, how they're going to get the power, their water usage, their carbon emissions, the efficiency of the datacenter, where it is going to be located physically, the noise levels of the facility, the water sources, which is a big one, and how much water they're going to use is another big one that operators have traditionally not been very forthright in publishing." In Virginia – the world's "datacenter capital" – an ex-water sustainability program manager at AWS is taking his former employer to court over claims it published false and misleading statements about water use in the state. item.title: China outlines plans for moonshot it hopes to land by 2030
item.description: China’s crewed space program has outlined plans for a moon landing it hopes to achieve by the year 2030. Deputy chief designer Wang Xiang explained the plans last weekend at an event called the Seventh Manned Space Symposium. Chinese state media has posted video of Wang discussing plans to reach Luna by launching two Long March 10 rockets. One will carry a lander named “Lanyue” and the other will hoist a crew capsule called “Mengzhou.” The two craft will meet in orbit around the Moon, where two of the three Taikonauts aboard Mengzhou will transfer to Lanyue and descend to set boot on regolith. In the video, Wang said China plans near-Earth orbit test missions for both vehicles in coming years, followed by an uncrewed visit to the Moon. If all goes well, China hopes to attempt a crewed landing by 2030. The Seventh Manned Space Symposium marked the 70th anniversary of the founding of China's space program and was also pitched as a moment for articulation of the nation’s ambitions in space under its 15 th five-year-plan, Beijing’s blueprint for the years 2026 to 2030. China called off its last moonshot in August, when authorities decided the Chang’e 7 robotic ice hunting mission “ failed to meet launch criteria ” just one day before its planned launch. The orbit required to reach the South Lunar Pole for that mission isn’t always easily accessible, so China plans to try again next year. When China tries to get Chang’e 7, Lanyue, and Mengzhou flying, it will at least have some new standards to apply to their operations after the China Manned Space Engineering Office last week published seventeen of them. One of the standards defines the architecture for Ethernet and Wi-Fi networks on China’s space station and other orbiters. Another governs signage used in orbit, in the hope that a standard means Taikonauts won’t make mistakes. A couple outline procedures for extravehicular activities, and use of a robotic arm to assist Taikonauts on such missions. Others explain the materials designers can choose from when building spacecraft. ®

item.title: Before the Dawn in America’s Heartland
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Before the Dawn in America’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 18, 2026 The predawn hours brought clear skies over much of the eastern United States on October 18, 2026. An astronaut aboard the International Space Station seized the opportunity to capture this wide-angle photo at 4:54 a.m. Central Daylight Time (09:54 Universal Time), with illuminated cities large and small arrayed across the darkened landscape. The U.S. Midwest’s largest metropolitan areas , such as Chicago, Illinois, and Detroit, Michigan, stand out as some of the brightest features. Mid-sized cities—including Indianapolis, Indiana; Cincinnati, Ohio; and Louisville, Kentucky—and their interconnections along state and interstate highways also shine brightly. Above the web of nighttime lights and Earth’s lower atmosphere, a diffuse layer of green and orange is visible along the horizon to the left. This band of light is airglow , produced when sunlight strikes atoms and molecules in the upper atmosphere and causes them to eject photons . To the right, light from the Sun arcs across the horizon; sunrise was about an hour away on the East Coast and about two hours away in Chicago. Astronaut photos and other remote sensing observations of nighttime lights are scientifically valuable for tracking changes in the built environment. For example, Chicago’s lightscape appears a homogeneous pale yellow in the wide view above. But in detailed photos, like the one below, a range of colors stemming from different types of lighting is discernible. Using NASA’s extensive Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth archive, researchers have developed a method for distinguishing lighting types within the pixels of nighttime photos. Systematically quantifying urban lights’ brightness, color, and extent can provide insight into how cities grow and evolve . March 1, 2024 Satellite sensors also observe changes to lighting. In particular, NASA’s Black Marble nighttime lights product suite uses satellite observations to produce science-quality records of nighttime lights across the globe at daily, monthly, and yearly time scales. In the eastern U.S., scientists have used these data to track everything from power outages and restoration following major storms to lighting changes associated with new infrastructure to transitions to LED lighting from older forms. item.title: AMD on track to overtake Intel as biggest x86 outfit
item.description: AMD has predicted it will win more revenue than Intel in its next quarter, potentially marking the first time it becomes the dominant vendor whose main product is x86 processors. The house of Zen on Tuesday announced its Q3 2026 results, which saw it grow revenue 45 percent year-over-year to $13.4 billion. The company’s Data Center segment won $8.5 billion of revenue, up 97 percent year-over-year. Sales of silicon in AMD’s client and gaming segment slid eight percent to $3.7 billion, a worse fall than the five percent fall that helped to sink Intel’s share price . Intel, AMD’s great rival in the x86 market, offered revenue guidance of $15 billion to $16 billion for its next quarter, which would represent almost no growth. AMD, by contrast, told investors it expects around $17 billion of revenue next quarter. CEO Lisa Su predicted even better days are ahead. “We think 2027 is going to be a very strong momentum year for both the CPU business as well as the data center AI business,” she said on the company’s earnings call. “We have said the overall company will grow greater than 80 percent, and for the data center CPU business, we will about double, and for the data center AI business, it will significantly more than double.” Su said AMD is confident its supply chain can meet that demand. “We have worked across our supply chain to secure the wafers, substrates, advanced packaging, memory, and other key components needed to support much higher growth next year,” she said. “We are also deepening our collaboration with our supply chain partners and investing alongside them to secure the long-term capacity our growth will require.” The CEO added that AMD has “strong confidence in our ability to sustain exceptional revenue growth for years to come, with earnings growing even faster.” If those predictions are correct, AMD will likely accelerate away from Intel to become the leading provider of x86 processors after years of challenging Chipzilla's lead. Intel would still have higher overall revenue, due to its foundry operations, but in terms of revenue earned from selling chips, AMD would become the market leader. AMD is arguably already the server CPU technology leader, and while it is second to Nvidia in the GPU market has trounced Intel. Even AMD's declining client and gaming revenue has an upside because it was the gaming part of the portfolio that created the problem. PC chip sales rose seven percent year-over-year to $2.9 billion. Su said strong sales of Ryzen mobile processors drove that growth. “Commercial is becoming a larger part of our client business as large enterprises adopt Ryzen PRO PCs across their employee base,” she said, pointing to strong adoption at the world’s largest banks, automotive companies, and healthcare concerns. Big corporate buyers are often a source of bigger profits and/or steadier revenue, so AMD looks to be taking the cream off the top of the PC market rather than scrounging for SMB and retail scraps.
